docs.x: Every FortiWeb ships the same set of predefined (factory) Web Protection Profiles, such as Inline Standard Protection . The Factory catalog stores each of them once per firmware version, build number and REST API version , the first time a deep rediscovery reads them. Later deep rediscoveries rebuild those profiles from the catalog instead of reading every sub-table from the appliance again. The page lets you browse the stored profiles, compare a profile between two builds and save one as a template.

Keeps one entry per predefined profile ( Inline WPP or Offline WPP ) per firmware build and API version. A newer build can add fields to the same profile, so each build has its own entries. Fills and reuses entries during the deep pass of a rediscovery : First deep pass on a build — reads the predefined profiles in full and stores the complete tree, every object it names and every read it made. docs.s: Compare how a published service is configured on two FortiWeb appliances — policy, virtual server, pool, certificates, content routing, allow lists and the web protection profile — from a simple source;policy;destination list, without writing anything.

docs.x: Config Compare checks whether a service is configured the same on two FortiWeb appliances, and if not, exactly what differs. You give it one line per service — source;policy;destination — and SATOM reads every object behind the server policy on both boxes and subtracts them. It is the natural check after cloning a policy or before a migration, and it writes nothing .

Reads the full dependency tree of the named server policy on the source and on the destination: virtual server, server pool and members, certificates, content routing, allow lists, the web protection profile and their sub-tables. Pairs objects by the field that references them , not by name. An object that landed under a different name on the destination is reported as renamed , not as one object missing plus another one added. Compares a web protection profile as one package : object counts and a fingerprint per side, −removed ~changed +added , and which sub-profiles differ — never one row pe

Both appliances are FortiWebs registered in SATOM and visible in the current ADOM. Each side is identified by its SATOM name or its host (not case-sensitive). SATOM must be able to reach both appliances' REST API — the comparison reads live, it does not use the local copy. No device needs to be selected and no workspace tab needs to be open.

Opening and running the page needs the legacy view permission, which any granular view key grants — for example network.view , protection.view , appliances.view , monitoring.view or operations.view . All system profiles, including Viewer , have it. A user with none of them gets the 403 page, and the sidebar entry is shown only to users who can open the page. Only appliances visible to you (current ADOM, maintenance rules) can be named in the list.

docs.h: Objects created by the line wizard do not use my patterns
docs.x: Possible causes - The patterns were saved for FortiADC, not FortiWeb. The wizard reads the FortiWeb catalog. - The plan was computed before you saved the patterns. Solution 1. docs.x: Possible causes - The page was opened without ?product=fortiadc . An unknown or missing product falls back to FortiWeb. Solution 1. Use the Product selector, or open /naming/?product=fortiadc . Verification - The breadcrumb ends in FortiADC , and the card title reads Patterns — FortiADC .

docs.h: A derived name is cut off
docs.x: Possible causes - The rendered name exceeds 63 characters. SATOM truncates it so the appliance accepts it. Solution 1. Shorten the fixed part of the pattern (prefixes or suffixes), or use shorter web addresses. Verification - The preview after → shows the full name with no truncation.

Advanced Storage Overrides are stored as JSON in the application settings: key naming.scheme for FortiWeb (the original key, kept for compatibility) and naming.scheme.<product> for other products. The product selector lists every device ADOM. An object type outside the catalog is stored in the same per-product key as table:<registry name> ; the flows that build names never read those. The first cut of Discovery kept adopted patterns apart, under naming.discovered.<product> . The page moves them into the scheme the first time it opens (unless the entry already has its own pattern) and logs it.

docs.s: The global catalog of AppIDs (billing key and access-control unit) and the binding of each server policy to exactly one AppID, fed by hand, by file upload or by a nightly URL import.

docs.x: An AppID is two things at once. It is a billing key : the customer a server policy is charged to. It is also an access-control unit : an API token can be pinned to AppIDs, so an external integrator only reaches the server policies bound to their AppIDs. The AppIDs page manages the catalog and the bindings. Both live in SATOM's own database, never in a file or a policy comment. Files and URLs are only sources that feed the catalog.

The page has four tabs: Catalog : add an AppID by hand, see every AppID with its source and status ( active , stale , inactive ) and how many policies are bound to it, and delete one. Upload & map : upload a CSV, TSV, TXT or PDF file, preview it, map its columns to fields once , and import. The mapping is saved and reused by later uploads and by the nightly import. Nightly source : configure a URL (with optional basic or bearer authentication) that the scheduled action appid_import fetches. Assign policies : bind a server policy on a device to an AppID, and remove bindings. Imports are additiv

For assignments: the appliance must be registered in SATOM and visible to you. Devices in maintenance mode are offered only if you hold appliances.view_maintenance . The server policy name is typed, not picked, so make sure it matches the policy name on the device exactly. For a FortiWeb, the policy must be in SATOM's local copy of the device configuration (last sync). For PDF uploads: the server needs the pdfplumber package. Without it the preview answers PDF import needs the 'pdfplumber' package, which is not installed. For the nightly import: a scheduled action of type Import AppID catalog

Every action on this page requires users.manage ( Administrator ). The Administrator menu group, and with it the AppIDs entry, is hidden from users without it. A direct request to /appids/ returns 403 Forbidden . ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: the Assign policies device picker and the assign/unassign actions cover only the appliances visible to you, assigning a FortiWeb policy checks that the device has it, and unticking First row is a header now works. The page is linked only from the Global ADOM. From the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles, the URL redirects to that console'
Open Administrator → AppIDs in the Global ADOM. The Catalog tab is shown. Fill AppID * and optionally Customer , Label and Rate . Click Add AppID . The flash reads AppID <id> created.

Open the Upload & map tab. Choose the File ( .csv , .tsv , .txt or .pdf ). Leave First row is a header ticked if the first row holds column names. Untick it for a file without a header row; columns are then referenced by index number and the first row is imported as data. Click Preview & map . The first rows appear in a table, together with any parser note (for example for PDFs). Under Map columns → fields , pick the AppID column * and, optionally, the Customer column , Label column and Rate column . Columns you saved previously are preselected. To keep more columns, click Add extra field , ty

Open the Nightly source tab. Set Source type to Fetch from URL (nightly) and enter the URL . Choose Auth : none , basic (fill Username (basic) and Password (basic) ) or bearer (fill Bearer token ). Click Save source . The flash reads External source + mapping saved. The nightly action will reuse it. Under Administrator → System → System Automations, create an Import AppID catalog (nightly) action. It reuses the URL and the saved column mapping. ℹ️ Note Do an upload with the same file layout first. The nightly import uses the column mapping saved by Import (additive) . It does not ask for one.

docs.h: Assign a server policy to an AppID
docs.x: Open the Assign policies tab. Pick the AppID * and the Device * , and type the Server Policy name * exactly as it is on the device. Click Assign . The flash reads Policy <name> assigned. For a FortiWeb, a name that is not in SATOM's local copy of the device is refused (see Troubleshooting ). If the policy was already bound to another AppID, the binding moves to the new one. A policy never has two AppIDs. To remove a binding, click the × button on its row in the table below. The flash reads Policy <name> unassigned.

On the Catalog tab, click the trash button on the row. Confirm Delete AppID <id> and its <n> policy binding(s)? The AppID and all its bindings are removed. The flash reads AppID <id> deleted (and its policy bindings).

Max. 200 characters No Web shop Rate Free text, max. 64 characters No 50 First row is a header Map columns by header name instead of position. 🧪 Example — Monthly billing file plus nightly refresh Finance publishes appids.csv with the columns AppID;Client;Service;Price;Env . An admin uploads it once and maps AppID column → AppID , Customer column → Client , Label column → Service and Rate column → Price , and adds the extra field environment → Env . The import reports 120 new, 0 updated, 0 newly stale, 0 skipped . The admin then saves the same file's URL as the nightly source with a bearer token and creates the scheduled action. A week later one AppID disappears from the file. The next nightly run marks it stale , and its policy bind

The catalog and bindings are stored in SATOM's database. Each action writes an audit entry: appid.create , appid.delete , appid.import (with the counts), appid.source_save , appid.assign and appid.unassign . An API token whose AppID scope lists AppIDs may only run backend, policy and certificate actions whose target server policy is bound to one of those AppIDs, and no fleet-wide action. Only bindings on appliances of the token's own product count.

Click Preview & map again and check the column names in the preview. 2. Pick the right AppID column and import again. Verification - The success flash reports a non-zero new or updated count.

Possible causes - An AppID with the same key exists already, possibly in different upper or lower case. Solution 1. Search the Catalog table for the key. Import a file instead if you want to update an existing entry. An import updates existing AppIDs. Verification - The catalog shows exactly one row for the key.

docs.h: A file without a header row loses its first line
docs.x: Possible causes - First row is a header was left ticked, so the first row was read as column names. Solution 1. Untick First row is a header , click Preview & map , map the columns by index and import again. The saved mapping keeps the setting for the nightly import. Verification - The import's new plus updated count equals the number of data rows.

docs.h: " has no server policy named ' ' in the local store. …"
docs.x: Possible causes - The name is misspelt, or the policy was created on the FortiWeb after the last device sync. Solution 1. Check the exact name on the device's Server Policy list. 2. If the policy is new, press Refresh from device on Server Policy and assign again. Verification - The flash reads Policy <name> assigned.

docs.h: The nightly action reports "AppID import skipped — no external URL source is configured (upload is manual-only)."
docs.x: Possible causes - Source type is still Manual upload only , or the URL is empty. Solution 1. Open Nightly source , choose Fetch from URL (nightly) , enter the URL and click Save source . Verification - The next run reports AppID import: <n> new, <n> updated, … .

docs.h: The nightly action reports "AppID import failed: …"
docs.x: Possible causes - The URL is unreachable, returned an HTTP error, or the credentials are wrong. - The file is a PDF and pdfplumber is missing. Solution 1. Fetch the URL from the SATOM host with the same credentials. 2. Re-enter the password or token and click Save source . Verification - The next run of the scheduled action reports a summary instead of an error.

Advanced Parsing, matching and storage Delimited files are sniffed for , , ; , tab and | . Ragged rows are padded. A PDF table is read page by page. A PDF without a table becomes a single text column, one line per row. With a header, a mapping reference is matched by header name (case-insensitive), then by column index as a fallback. An import never blanks a field: an empty cell keeps the stored value. Extra fields are merged into the AppID's existing extra values. The mapping and source are stored in the application settings under appid.import.global . Password and token are Fernet-encrypted,

docs.s: The Zones, Lines and Departments catalogs used to classify appliances, where renaming a value moves every reference and removing one asks where its references go.

docs.x: Device Classification holds three catalogs: Network Zones : where an appliance sits (for example dmz , internal ). Lines : the service line or environment (for example production , staging ). Departments : the owning team or function. Each appliance is given one value per catalog on its Edit page. The same values group devices on the Architecture map and in the bookmarks rail. They also scope configuration baselines, network segments and line profiles . Despite its place under this category, the page is not specific to FortiWeb. It is a console-wide administration page.

The page edits one row per value , not a free-text list. That lets SATOM tell a rename from a delete: Rename a value: every appliance, baseline combo, network segment and line profile that uses the old value is moved to the new one in the same save. Remove a value that is in use: the save is refused until you choose, per value, under Move its references to: , whether its references are cleared ( Clear them (leave unclassified) ) or moved to another value of the same catalog. In use by shows, per value, how many appliances ( appl. ), baseline combos ( combo ), network segments ( seg. ) and, for
None. The catalogs can be filled before any appliance exists.

users.manage is required to view and save ( Administrator ). The entry sits in the Administrator group, which is hidden without it, and /classification/ answers 403 Forbidden to other users. The menu entry is in the Global ADOM. From the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles the URL redirects to that console's home page.
Open Administrator → Classification in the Global ADOM. In the card of the catalog ( Network Zones , Lines or Departments ), click Add value and type the value. Click Save Classification .
Edit the text of the value in place. Click Save Classification . When references moved, the flash reads Classification saved. <n> reference(s) updated.

Click Remove on its row. The row is struck through, and a value that was never saved disappears at once. If the value is in use, choose under Move its references to: either Clear them (leave unclassified) or another value. The list offers the catalog's current values, including names you just typed. Click Save Classification . Click Undo on a removed row to keep it after all.

Field Description Required Example Value The catalog entry. Unique per catalog, compared case-insensitively Yes dmz Move its references to: For a removed value: — choose — (no decision), Clear them (leave unclassified) , or another value Yes, when the value is in use internal

🧪 Example — Normalising a zone name Appliances were classified with the zone internal , and the team wants Internal . The admin edits the row to Internal and saves. SATOM moves the appliances, the baselines and the segments that held internal to Internal in one transaction. An automatically named baseline combo is renamed to match its new zone. If a combo for the new value already exists, the old combo is merged into it, and the flash adds <n> duplicate combo(s) absorbed .

The catalogs are saved, and references are moved, cleared or reassigned in the same transaction. Clearing a line that has a line profile deletes that profile, because a profile without a line answers for nothing. The Audit Log records classification.save with +added ~renamed -deleted per catalog and the number of references touched. A refused save is recorded as classification.refused .

When a save is refused, the page comes back with your edits, not the stored catalog, so you can correct and resubmit. Every refusal message starts with the catalog name ( zones: , lines: or departments: ).

docs.h: "' ' is still used by appliance(s), baseline(s), segment(s) and line profile(s). Choose what happens to them before removing it."
docs.x: Possible causes - You removed a value that records still use, and left Move its references to: on — choose — . - For Lines , the value may be used only by a line profile; the message then counts it under line profile(s) . ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: the refusal message and the In use by badges now count line profiles; before, a line used only by a line profile was refused with all counts at 0 . Solution 1. Pick Clear them (leave unclassified) or a replacement value. 2. Save again. Verification - The flash reads Classification saved. <n> reference(s) updated.

docs.h: "Cannot rename ' ' to ' ' in the same save that also changes ' '. Do it in two steps."
docs.x: Possible causes - You swapped two values, or renamed a value onto a name that is itself being renamed or removed. Solution 1. Rename one value to a temporary name and save. 2. Do the second rename and save again. Verification - Each step saves without a refusal.

docs.h: "' ' is listed twice (also as ' '). Values must be unique."
docs.x: Possible causes - Two rows hold the same value, possibly in different case. Solution 1. Remove or rename one of them. Verification - The save succeeds.

docs.h: "' ' is no longer in the catalog — it changed while this page was open. Reload and retry."
docs.x: Possible causes - Another admin saved the catalog after you opened the page. Solution 1. Reload the page and repeat your edits. Verification - The save succeeds.

docs.h: "combo ' ' would merge into ' ', but it has template(s) that combo does not. Reassign or delete that combo first."
docs.x: Possible causes - The rename would make two baseline combos describe the same zone, line and department, and the one being absorbed has templates the other lacks. Solution 1. Open the baseline combos under System provisioning profiles , and move or remove the extra templates. 2. Save the classification again. Verification - The save succeeds and reports the combo as absorbed.

docs.h: "line ' ' already has a profile in product ' ', and ' ' has one too. …"
docs.x: Possible causes - Both lines have a line profile in the same product, so they cannot be merged. Solution 1. Delete or edit one of the two line profiles. 2. Save the classification again. Verification - The save succeeds.

Advanced How references are stored and moved Zone, line and department are plain strings on appliances, on baselines and inside each network segment. There is no foreign key. That is why this page moves references explicitly. Usage counts compare the exact stored string. dmz and DMZ are different values to the database, so they are counted separately. A catalog value that the form did not send back is treated as a removal and goes through the same reference check. A segment carries one zone and one line but a list of departments. Renaming a department rewrites it in that list.

docs.s: Declare, per classification line, which network segments it receives, which certificate class and which Web Protection Profile template a new server policy on that line starts from.

docs.x: A line profile states what one classification line (for example production ) receives: the network segments a new policy on that line may be placed in, the certificate class its certificate is issued under, the Web Protection Profile template it starts from, optionally an IPAM pool to take addresses from. The New Server Policy from a line wizard reads these declarations. A line without a profile still works, but SATOM then infers its segments by matching each segment's line field to the line name, and the page labels that answer as a guess.

Shows one card per value of the Lines catalog (from Classification ), with a badge: declared (a profile exists) or inferred — no profile . Lists the line's Resolved segments and every problem found, each with a code. Problems that would stop policy creation are red, and the card shows blocks policy creation . Lets you create, update or delete the profile of each line.

Code Meaning Blocks policy creation missing_segment The profile names a segment that no longer exists Yes no_segments No network segment is assigned to the line Yes duplicate_segment Two segments share a name, so the network is ambiguous Yes wpp_gone The named WPP template no longer exists Yes wpp_not_approved The WPP template is not approved Yes wpp_wrong_product The WPP template belongs to another product Yes no_cert_class No certificate class is declared No (the wizard asks) no_wpp No WPP template is named No segment_no_cidr A segment has no CIDR, so no address can be allocated from it No A

At least one value in the Lines catalog ( Classification ). With an empty catalog the page says The Lines catalog is empty. Add lines in Classification first — a profile can only answer for a line that exists. Network segments defined under Network Segments ( Segments ). Optionally, an approved FortiWeb web-protection-profile template in the Template Library .

users.manage is required to view, save and delete ( Administrator ). Without it the Administrator menu group is hidden and /line-profiles/ answers 403 Forbidden . From the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles the URL redirects to that console's home page. ❗ Important — Profiles are FortiWeb profiles The menu entry is in the Global ADOM, but the page always runs in the FortiWeb ADOM: opening it from Global switches that browser tab to FortiWeb. Profiles are therefore stored as FortiWeb profiles, which is what the line wizard reads, and the template list offers the FortiWeb We

Open Global ADOM → Administrator → Line Profiles . The page runs in the FortiWeb ADOM (see the note above). Find the card of the line. In Segments this line receives , select one or more segments (use Ctrl or Cmd to select several). Choose the Certificate class ( server , clientserver or client ), or leave — not decided — . Optionally fill IPAM pool override . When it is blank, the segment's CIDR is used. Choose the Web Protection Profile template . Each option shows the name, version and status. Only an approved template can be used to build a policy. Optionally add a Note . Click Save profil

On the line's card, click Delete profile (falls back to the guess) . The flash reads Profile for '<line>' deleted — this line falls back to matching segments by name, which is a guess, not a declaration. The buttons Network segments and Classification at the top of the page open the two pages a profile depends on.

Field Description Required Example Segments this line receives Network segments by name. Unknown names are refused No dmz-web Certificate class server , clientserver or client . Blank = not decided No server IPAM pool override Pool to allocate addresses from instead of the segment CIDR. Max. 128 characters No 192.0.2.0/26 Web Protection Profile template A web-protection-profile template of this product No wpp-baseline v3 — approved Note Free text, max. 2,000 characters No Owned by the web team

🧪 Example — Declaring the production line The Lines catalog contains production . Two segments, dmz-web ( 192.0.2.0/24 ) and dmz-api ( 198.51.100.0/24 ), carry line=production . Without a profile, the card shows inferred — no profile and both segments. The admin opens Line Profiles , selects only dmz-web , picks certificate class server and the approved template wpp-baseline v3 — approved , and saves. The card turns declared , and the wizard now offers only dmz-web for production policies, with that template.

The profile is stored for (product, line). One profile per line and product. The wizard uses it for every new policy on that line. Renaming the line in Classification moves the profile with it. Clearing the line's references deletes the profile. The Audit Log records line_profile.save (with the segment count, certificate class and template id) and line_profile.delete .

docs.h: The wizard still says "No profile for this line" after I saved one
docs.x: Possible causes - A profile saved under the Global ADOM before 2.11.0 was not moved at startup, because FortiWeb already had a profile for the same line. The wizard reads the FortiWeb profile. - The line of the wizard run is not the line you declared. Solution 1. Open Line Profiles and check the card of the line the wizard uses. 2. Declare or correct the profile there and save. Verification - The card shows declared , and the wizard no longer shows the inferred warning for that line.

Possible causes - A selected segment was renamed or deleted on the Network Segments page while this page was open. Solution 1. Reload the page and select the segments again. Verification - The save flash reads Line profile for '<line>' created. or updated.

docs.h: "' ' is not in the Lines catalog."
docs.x: Possible causes - The line was renamed or removed in Classification after the page loaded. Solution 1. Reload the page. Only current lines have cards. Verification - The card for the line is present after reload.

docs.h: "That Web Protection Profile template does not belong to this product."
docs.x: Possible causes - The submitted template is not a FortiWeb Web Protection Profile template. Solution 1. Reload the page and choose a template from the list. The list offers only FortiWeb Web Protection Profile templates. Verification - The save succeeds and the card shows no wpp_wrong_product problem.

docs.h: The card shows blocks policy creation with wpp_not_approved
docs.x: Possible causes - The named template is pending or was rejected. Solution 1. Have an administrator approve it in the Template Library , or pick an approved template. Verification - The wpp_not_approved problem disappears from the card.

Advanced How the plan is computed services/line_profiles.line_plan is the only place the answer is computed. This page and the wizard both call it. A declared profile never falls back to the inferred match. A profile whose segments no longer resolve stays declared , with missing_segment problems. Segments are stored by name , in order, without duplicates. The segments list is rewritten whole on every edit, so names are more stable than positions. The address pool used by the wizard is the profile's IPAM pool override if set, else the chosen segment's CIDR. With neither, the wizard must ask.

docs.s: The dependency tree of FortiWeb objects that hang off a server policy or a Web Protection Profile, cross-referenced against the endpoint registry, a chosen firmware build and the CLI configuration dump.

docs.x: Object Structure & Dependencies is a reference page in the API area. It shows how FortiWeb objects depend on each other, starting from a Server Policy or a Web Protection Profile . For each object it also shows whether SATOM's endpoint registry covers it, whether a chosen firmware build serves it, and whether it appears in a captured CLI configuration dump. The page belongs to the API registry tooling rather than to day-to-day policy work. Use it to understand what a policy clone has to carry and where the API catalog has gaps.

Coverage tiles : In registry (tree nodes whose URN matches a registry endpoint), Fetchable (URN) nodes , Missing from registry and Coverage as a percentage of the fetchable nodes. Dependency Tree : the tree of objects and sub-elements as text, with a Copy button. Show URNs / Hide URNs toggles the REST paths in the tree. Registry Cross-Reference : one row per tree node, with FortiWeb object , URN (REST) , In registry? ( Missing , the matching endpoint, or grouping for a node without a URN), Serves it? , Served by (a transport badge from the CLI evidence) and Test . A filter box narrows the rows

Choose a build in the Firmware selector to fill this column: Badge Meaning served A sweep of this build answered for the endpoint partial For a line rollup: only some builds of the line served it (hover for the list) absent on this build The build was asked and does not serve it could not ask The sweep recorded an error unmeasured No sweep of this build ever asked about the endpoint — No firmware chosen, or the node has no URN

The endpoint registry is installed (it is part of SATOM). For Serves it? : API sweeps recorded for the firmware build or line you pick. The selector lists the FortiWeb builds and lines in SATOM's API version matrix. For the CLI sections: a captured CLI configuration dump of a FortiWeb. Without one, the card says that no dump has been captured and that this is an absence of evidence, not a finding.

Viewing the page needs users.manage ( Administrator ), the same as its only way in, the API entry at the bottom of the FortiWeb ADOM sidebar. Other users get 403 Forbidden . Structure Overlay (admin) is shown and saved only with users.manage ( Administrator ). Other users don't see the card, and a direct save returns 403 Forbidden . The Test buttons call other pages' endpoints and inherit their checks. API runs a GET through the API explorer, which needs registry.view . CLI runs a live show <path> and needs the legacy backup permission, which backups.create or backups.restore grants. ℹ️ Note C

docs.h: Read the coverage of the tree
docs.x: In the FortiWeb ADOM, click API in the sidebar, then the Structure tab next to API-Registry Explorer . Read the four tiles, then scan Registry Cross-Reference for Missing rows. Type in Filter objects by name, URN or section… to find one object.

Choose a version or a line rollup in the Firmware selector. The page reloads with that build; the Apply button next to the selector does the same. Read Serves it? for the rows you care about. The choice is part of the address ( ?scope=<version> , for example ?scope=7.6.4 , or a line such as ?scope=7.6 ), so the view can be bookmarked.

docs.h: Test one row against a live appliance
docs.x: Click API (or CLI in the CLI-only table) in the row's Test column. The Test against a live appliance dialog opens. Choose the Appliance (FortiWebs you can see), then press API or CLI on the row again. The test is read-only: a GET , or show , never a write.

Scroll to Structure Overlay (admin) . Enter a JSON object with any of the keys added , edited , removed , order and functions . Do not store secrets here. Click Save overlay . The flash reads Structure overlay saved. To return to the built-in tree, click Restore defaults and confirm Reset the structure overlay to the built-in defaults? . Saving an empty overlay clears it too ( Structure overlay cleared. ).

🧪 Example — Is a new object type cloneable on 7.6? An engineer wants to know whether a profile feature can be cloned between two FortiWebs on the same build. On Structure , they pick that build in Firmware and filter the cross-reference for the feature name. The row shows the URN, In registry? with the endpoint name and Serves it? = served , so that build exposes it over REST. In CLI-only elements , a related block appears in the clone-gap warning with 3 rows . That configuration exists only in the CLI and will be missing on a cloned device.
Viewing changes nothing. Saving or resetting the overlay writes the application setting structure.overlay and an audit entry structure.save with the number of added, edited and removed nodes.

docs.h: Serves it? shows only — after choosing a firmware
docs.x: Possible causes - No firmware is chosen (the selector is on none chosen — CLI evidence unfiltered ), or the page was not reloaded. Solution 1. Choose the build again, or press Apply next to the selector. 2. Alternatively, open /structure/?scope=<version> . Add &urns=1 to keep URNs visible. Verification - The Firmware selector shows the chosen build, and Serves it? has badges instead of — .

docs.h: "Invalid overlay: overlay must be a JSON object"
docs.x: Possible causes - The text is valid JSON but not an object (for example a list), or it is not valid JSON at all (the message then names the parser error). Solution 1. Wrap the content in { … } and use the documented keys. Verification - The flash reads Structure overlay saved. , and the overlay card shows the active badge.

Possible causes - No CLI configuration dump of a FortiWeb has been captured. - The chosen firmware has no dump. A build never borrows another build's evidence. Solution 1. Capture a CLI dump from the API hub, then reload. 2. Or remove scope= from the address (the selector's none chosen — CLI evidence unfiltered ) to use whichever dump exists. Verification - The CLI-only card header names the device, version and capture date of the evidence.

Advanced Where the data comes from The tree is a hand-authored dependency map ( app/registry/dependencies ), not a measurement. It is the same for every build. Only the Serves it? and CLI columns change with the selected firmware. The registry cross-reference reads the pure registry ( get_registry_endpoints ). CLI-only nodes hang from their own root on purpose: a CLI block has no via edge, and grafting it into the policy subtree would suggest a clone path that the appliance rejects. The clone-gap list is capped at 20 entries on screen. The table below it holds all of them.

docs.s: Register the Fortinet appliances SATOM manages, keep their credentials and documentation up to date, and open each device's page for every device-level action.

docs.x: Appliances is SATOM's inventory of the Fortinet devices it manages: FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate (on FortiGate, SATOM edits only from the measured GUI pages and the dry-run API console — see FortiGate ). Each row stores how SATOM reaches the device (host, port, credentials, TLS verification) plus documentation you add yourself (tags, classification, model, interfaces, a datasheet). Every device-level action — discovery, console, backups, firmware, HA failover — starts from the appliance's own page.

Lists every appliance you are allowed to see, with a live Online / Offline status badge. Adds, edits and deletes appliance records. Credentials are stored encrypted. Tests the connection to a device on demand. Folds the several rows of one multi-ADOM FortiWeb into one device line, and keeps the device-wide actions on one of those rows only. Puts a device into maintenance mode , which hides it from operators and read-only users. Documents the physical side of a device: hardware or VM, model, datasheet PDF and its interfaces with their role. Gives each appliance a detail page with quick actions,

The device's management interface must be reachable from the SATOM node over HTTPS (default port 443). An administrator account on the device. For a FortiWeb in ADOM mode, the account and the ADOM you enter decide which partition SATOM sees. FortiAuthenticator authenticates with a per-user API key , not the login password. Issue one by ticking Web service access on an administrator account on the FortiAuthenticator, and store that key in the Password field. If Verify SSL certificate stays ticked, the device's certificate must chain to a public root or to a CA imported in the Trust store .

Action What unlocks it Open the appliance list and a device page, run Test Connection , open a datasheet, read the live HA member roles, open the Firmware Reports pages appliances.view See the Appliances menu entry (in the Administrator group for holders of users.manage ; otherwise in the Operations group of a product ADOM, in the Global group of the Global ADOM) appliances.view Add Appliance , Edit , Delete , add or detach HA members appliances.edit . The routes check the legacy config_write key, so appliances.apply or any other edit/apply permission (for example protection.edit ) also unlock

Open Appliances (in the Administrator group; without the administrator capability, in the Operations group, or the Global group in the Global ADOM) and click Add Appliance . Fill in Name , Kind , Host / IP , Port , Username and Password (all marked with a red asterisk except Port). If the device is a FortiWeb with ADOMs enabled, type the ADOM in ADOM (vdom, optional) . Leave it empty when ADOMs are off. For a FortiGate, this field is the VDOM to read. FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate take an API key or token in Password , not a login password: a FortiAuthenticator per-user API key, or a FortiG

In the list, click the lightning icon ( Test Connection ) on a row. The status badge turns Online or Offline and a toast says Connection successful or Connection failed . On the device page, click Test Connection . The page shows Connection OK , or Connection failed: followed by the device's error.

You can edit from two places: The pencil icon in the list opens a short Edit Appliance dialog: name, kind, host, port, username, password, ADOM (vdom), tags, classification, SSL verification and (for administrators) maintenance mode. Edit on the device page opens the full edit page, which also carries High Availability , Physical / Inventory (type, model, datasheet) and Interfaces / Connections . Leave New Password (leave blank to keep) empty to keep the stored password. Click Save Changes . Changing where the device is reached needs the password again. docs.h: Put a device into maintenance mode
docs.x: Administrators with appliances.view_maintenance see a tools icon on each row and an Enter maintenance / Leave maintenance button on the device page. Click Enter maintenance and confirm the prompt. The device gets a Maintenance badge and disappears for operators and read-only users. Scheduled probes and metric collection skip it. Click Leave maintenance to make it visible again. Monitoring is provisioned again for it. The button posts the state you want, not a toggle. If another administrator already changed it, you see fweb-01 is already in maintenance mode. and nothing else happens.

Click the trash icon on the row and confirm Delete appliance 'fweb-01'? This cannot be undone. SATOM records the device's identity first, then removes the row, its datasheet and its documented interfaces. The message reads Appliance fweb-01 deleted. Its identity, configuration history and backups on the server are kept — see Administration → Stored Assets. See Stored assets .

A FortiWeb in ADOM mode is registered once per ADOM (one row per ADOM, same host and port), because the login token carries exactly one ADOM. SATOM recognises rows with the same kind, host and port as one physical device: The list shows the device once, with an ADOM · n badge. Click the chevron to unfold the other ADOM rows. The Devices tile counts physical devices; the ADOMs tile counts the ADOM rows. Firmware, the backup vault and the console act on the whole box, so they live on one row: the row whose ADOM is root (or empty), otherwise the first row by name. The other rows show a link to it

Card What it shows Details Kind, host and port (with a link to open the device itself when one can be built), username, SSL verification, last known firmware, ADOM (vdom), department, zone Quick Actions FortiWeb: Browse Server Policies , View Backups , Analysis / FortiView . FortiADC: Browse Virtual Servers , View Backups , API Console . View Backups needs backups.view . Jobs on this device The running and most recent jobs (up to 8) for this appliance, with status, progress, user and start time. Refreshes every 2 seconds while a job is active, every 15 seconds otherwise. All jobs → opens the J

Policy Inspector reads every server policy live over REST and prints a tree per policy: virtual server and VIPs, server pool and back-ends, health check and web-protection profile. Raw JSON expands the full data. On a FortiADC, VS Inspector does the same per virtual server (listener, real-server pool and members, content routing and rewriting, certificate chain, WAF profile). Live mode follows each virtual server's references and reads only what it reaches; From last rediscovery draws the same tree from the last full-depth capture without contacting the device. In Global, Add Appliance : Name fweb-01 , Kind FortiWeb, Host 192.0.2.10 , ADOM (vdom) root . Add Appliance again: Name fweb-01-shop , same host and credentials, ADOM (vdom) adom_shop . Adding, editing, deleting and toggling maintenance write audit entries appliance.create , appliance.update , appliance.delete and appliance.maintenance . A connection test writes appliance.test (device page) or api.appliance.test (list). Adding or editing a device, or taking it out of maintenance, provisions metric collectors and threshold probes for it. Existing targets are never touched. The list's status badges are refreshed every 30 seconds. A cached status older than 20 seconds is probed again (6-second timeout per device).

Possible causes - Wrong username or password (for FortiAuthenticator: the API key) on the appliance record. - The ADOM (vdom) field names an ADOM while ADOMs are off on the device, or the other way round. - The administrator account is locked out after repeated failed logins. - The account's trusted hosts do not include the SATOM node. Solution 1. Open the device page, Edit , and re-enter the password (or API key). 2. Check the ADOM (vdom) field against the device's ADOM setting. 3. Unlock the account on the device, or wait for its lockout to expire, before testing again: every further attempt

docs.h: A new appliance stays Offline or never syncs
docs.x: Possible causes - The device presents a self-signed or privately signed certificate and Verify SSL certificate is ticked. The connection fails during the TLS handshake, before any login. - The management port or host is wrong, or a firewall blocks the SATOM node. Solution 1. Import the device's CA in Trust store , or untick Verify SSL certificate for that appliance. 2. Check host and port. Verification — the badge turns Online within 30 seconds, or immediately after Test Connection .

docs.h: "This ADOM can only add FortiADC appliances."
docs.x: Possible causes — You are in a product ADOM, which can only create appliances of its own product. Solution — Switch to the Global ADOM to add another product, or pick the ADOM of that product. Verification — The Kind list offers the product you need.
Possible causes — Names are unique across all ADOMs, including devices you cannot see (another product, or maintenance mode). Solution — Choose another name.

docs.h: "Datasheet must be a .pdf file." / "Datasheet exceeds the 25 MB limit."
docs.x: Possible causes — The upload is not a PDF, is empty ( Uploaded datasheet is empty. ), is larger than 25 MB, or does not start like a PDF ( File does not look like a valid PDF. ). Solution — Upload the vendor PDF datasheet, at most 25 MB.

docs.h: The interfaces of an appliance disappeared after an edit
docs.x: Possible causes — The appliance was saved from its full edit page with interface rows removed or left with an empty name. That page replaces all interface rows with the ones on the form. (The list's quick Edit Appliance dialog never changes interfaces.) Solution — Re-enter them on the full edit page, or run a Rediscovery to re-create name, type and IP (roles must be declared again by hand).

docs.h: A device someone else registered is missing from the list
docs.x: Possible causes — The device is in maintenance mode, or belongs to another product's ADOM. Solution — Ask an administrator with appliances.view_maintenance , or switch to the Global ADOM.

Advanced Where things are stored Credentials are encrypted in the database. The password is never shown again; the edit form only replaces it. The datasheet file is stored on the node by appliance id; the database keeps the original filename. Deleting an appliance removes everything that hangs off its database row (interfaces and other per-appliance records). Before that, SATOM records the device identity (serial, model) separately so backups on the external backup server keep an owner. Advanced How visibility is enforced Every user-facing list and every by-id page goes through the same visibi

docs.k: ha high availability cluster node 0 member primary secondary vip per-node failover failover set failover unset active-passive ha pair switchover role swap force standby appliances.edit appliances.view appliances.apply
docs.s: Model an appliance HA pair as one cluster with member nodes, see each member's live role, and hand the primary role over (failover) inside an approved change window.

docs.x: SATOM can model an appliance HA pair as one cluster . The cluster itself is a logical row called node 0 ; the real boxes are member nodes attached to it. Writes made through the cluster go to whichever member is primary. From the cluster's page you can also hand the primary role over to the peer ( HA Failover ) — but a live failover only runs inside an approved change request's window. ℹ️ Note This is SATOM's own model of the cluster: what you registered. The HA posture the devices report is shown separately on Device health under Device HA posture .

Lets you mark an appliance as an HA cluster (node 0) in one of two modes: Per-node IP — node 0 has no address of its own. Before each write SATOM asks the members which one is primary and writes there. Shared VIP — node 0's address is the cluster's shared management VIP, which always lands on the primary. Adds member nodes and detaches them again (a detached member becomes a standalone appliance). Shows each member's live role ( primary , secondary or unknown ) on the cluster page and in the appliance list. On the HA Failover page: runs a readiness check that sends nothing, runs a live failove

The cluster members must be reachable and their credentials valid for the live role to show. Failover is only offered for products whose failover command SATOM has verified: FortiWeb from firmware 8.0.0 and FortiADC from 7.6.0 . FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator are not supported. SATOM must know the firmware the target runs. A row with no recorded firmware is refused by the readiness check — run a Rediscovery or a device sync first. A live failover needs a change request for the action ha_failover that names this appliance, is approved (or scheduled / in progress) and whose window is open

Action Permission See the cluster card, members and live roles appliances.view (and the appliance must be visible to you) Mark a row as a cluster, add or detach members appliances.edit (legacy config_write ; any edit/apply permission also unlocks it) Open HA Failover , run the readiness check, fail over, plan a failover appliances.apply ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: HA Failover now requires appliances.apply (any edit permission no longer unlocks it), and the cluster page and live member roles require appliances.view . 🔑 Permission — Without the permission Without an edit permission, the HA Failov

Add Appliance (or edit an existing row on its full edit page — the list's quick Edit dialog does not carry the HA fields and leaves them unchanged). Tick This is an HA cluster (node 0) . Pick HA mode : - Per-node IP (detect live primary before each write) — leave Host empty if you like; members carry the addresses. - Shared VIP (one address that lands on the primary) — enter Shared VIP address . It becomes node 0's host. Save. Node 0 appears in the list with an HA · 0 badge.

Open node 0's page. The HA Cluster — members card shows the mode ( per_node or vip ). Fill in Member name , Host / mgmt IP , Username , Password and Role ( P1 = primary, P2 = secondary), then click the + button. The member inherits node 0's kind, SSL setting, ADOM (vdom), zone, line and department. In per-node mode the member's host is the address writes go through when that member is primary. In VIP mode it is the member's own management IP, used for read-only telemetry. A new member gets monitoring provisioned, like any appliance. Members are listed indented under their cluster in the applia

Click the detach icon on a member and confirm Detach member fweb-01b (it becomes standalone)? . The member becomes an ordinary appliance again: Cluster member detached (now standalone). To remove it completely, delete it afterwards from the appliance list. The page offers no way to attach an existing standalone appliance as a member; add the member with its own name and address instead.

On node 0's page (or a member's page), click HA Failover . The Transport card shows the exact CLI commands SATOM will send for Hand the role over and Give it back , the Minimum firmware , and the firmware recorded for this appliance. On FortiADC it warns that the forced state is sticky : it does not clear on reboot until an unset runs. Under Run now , pick Direction : set — hand the primary role to the peer or unset — give the role back / clear a forced failover . Click Readiness check . It runs the action's own dry run and sends nothing. It walks the same checks the live run makes (product, f

Make sure the page shows Authorised by CR-… — the change request whose window is open now. Otherwise it shows Live failover is blocked. with the reason, and the Fail over button is disabled. Pick the direction, type the appliance name in Type the appliance name to confirm a live run , and click Fail over . Confirm the prompt Fail over fweb-ha now? Every session on the outgoing primary breaks. SATOM moves the change request to in progress , sends the command over SSH, and closes the change with the real outcome. The result is shown under Result — LIVE set .

Under Plan it (raise a change request) , fill in Title , Direction , Risk , Window start , Window end , Responsible , Notify (e-mail) , Reason and Rollback , then click Raise change request . It is created as a draft : CR-… raised as a draft — approve and schedule it to make it run. You are taken to the change request. The direction travels with the change, so rescheduling keeps it.

Field Description Required Example This is an HA cluster (node 0) Makes the row a cluster container — ticked HA mode per_node (detect live primary) or vip (shared VIP) Yes for a cluster Per-node IP Shared VIP address The cluster's management VIP; becomes node 0's host Yes in VIP mode 192.0.2.50 Member name Unique appliance name of the member Yes fweb-01a Host / mgmt IP Member's management address Yes 192.0.2.11 Role Identity hint: P1 (primary) or P2 (secondary). The live role is read from the device. No P1 Direction (failover) set hands the role over, unset gives it back. Never defaulted. Yes

🧪 Example — Swapping the primary of a FortiWeb pair during a window fweb-ha is a per-node cluster with members fweb-01a (P1) and fweb-01b (P2), both on FortiWeb 8.0. On fweb-ha , HA Failover → Plan it : Direction set , window tonight 22:00–23:00. Raise change request . Approve and schedule the change on its page. At 22:05, open HA Failover again: the page reads Authorised by CR-… . Run Readiness check with set ; it reports which member is primary. Type fweb-ha , click Fail over . The change closes with the outcome. To return the role later, run unset under another approved change.

Audit entries: appliance.member_add , appliance.member_detach , appliance.failover_preflight , appliance.failover (with direction and change reference), appliance.failover_refused , appliance.failover_plan . A live failover starts and finishes its change request; the change's history records the outcome.

docs.h: "Live failover refused — change control: no approved change request names this appliance for ha_failover"
docs.x: Possible causes — No change request for ha_failover names this appliance, or none is approved, or its window is not open now. The message names the closest change and why it does not authorise. Solution 1. Plan the failover on this page, or open the named change request. 2. Get it approved and scheduled, and run the failover inside its window. Verification — The page shows Authorised by CR-… and Fail over is enabled.

docs.h: "fweb-01 is not registered as an HA cluster, so there is no peer to hand the primary role to."
docs.x: Possible causes — The row is neither a cluster node 0 nor a member. Solution — Mark it as a cluster (or attach it to one as a member node) under Edit , then plan the failover.

docs.h: "A live failover requires typing the exact appliance name to confirm. Nothing was sent."
docs.x: Solution — Type the appliance name exactly as shown in the page title.

docs.h: "Pick set (hand the role over) or unset (give it back). Nothing was sent."
docs.x: Solution — Select a direction. SATOM never assumes one.

docs.h: "SATOM has no recorded firmware version, and this command only exists from fortiweb 8.0.0"
docs.x: Possible causes — The node that would receive the command (the live primary in per-node mode) has no firmware recorded in SATOM. Solution — Run Sync device to local source of truth (a scheduled action) or a Rediscovery against that node, then repeat the readiness check. Verification — The readiness check passes the firmware step; the Transport card shows the recorded firmware.

docs.h: "refusing to fail over a node that reports 'secondary', not 'primary'"
docs.x: Possible causes — set was aimed at a node that is not the primary. Failing over a standby either does nothing or pins it out of HA election. Solution — Run the failover against the cluster (node 0) or against the member that is currently primary.
Possible causes — No failover command has been verified for this product, so nothing is offered. Solution — Fail over from the device itself.

Possible causes — The member is unreachable, its credentials fail, or the device answered without HA data. The role query times out after 5 seconds on the cluster page. Solution — Run Test Connection on the member's own page.

Advanced How the write target is chosen In VIP mode every write goes to node 0's host (the VIP). In per-node mode SATOM asks each member for its live role and writes to the one reporting primary ; if none can be reached, the write fails rather than guessing. Advanced Same gate as the scheduler The button on this page and the scheduled ha_failover action use the same change-control check. A readiness check is never gated: it reads the device and writes nothing.

docs.s: Read an appliance's entire configuration in one read-only sweep, refresh SATOM's cache and inventory from it, and optionally capture the full policy depth and the CLI configuration.

docs.x: Discovery (the first time) or Rediscovery (every time after) is a single read-only pass that asks a FortiWeb or FortiADC for every configuration object SATOM knows how to read. The result becomes the device's latest configuration snapshot, refreshes SATOM's local cache and fills in the appliance's model, firmware and interfaces. Two optional passes can follow: a deep capture (FortiWeb: every server policy and web-protection profile; FortiADC: every child table), and a CLI capture of show full-configuration over SSH.

Sends a GET to every top-level configuration endpoint in the endpoint registry (FortiADC: the FortiADC discovery plan). Sub-tables that need a parent key are skipped; the Policy Inspector / VS Inspector and the deep capture cover those. Classifies every answer: ok (the device answered — an empty list really is empty), absent (this firmware does not serve the path) or error (anything else). Writes a configuration snapshot, and keeps one copy per firmware version so an upgrade never overwrites the evidence of the previous version. Feeds the local cache as a harvest (trigger rediscovery ), so Dev

An appliance of kind FortiWeb or FortiADC . The deep capture differs per product: policy and WPP depth on FortiWeb, every child table on FortiADC. Working credentials. On FortiWeb and FortiADC a credential failure stops the sweep at once (see Troubleshooting ). For the CLI capture: SSH access to the device with the same credentials, and permission to write to the configuration vault.

With Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) on, after the sweep SATOM walks every server policy and web-protection profile (WPP) — sub-tables, rule lists, disabled signatures, exceptions — plus certificates and SNI, and stores the result as the device's deep layer. This is what the Analysis pages and the policy detail pages read. The WPPs are walked first, and every device read goes through a memo that lasts for the sweep: a server policy that names a WPP already walked is answered from the memo instead of reading that WPP's subtree again. On a FortiADC the switch is Capture full depth: every child table (REST) . After the sweep, SATOM reads each registered <parent>_child_<table> table once per parent object of the sweep ( ?pkey=<parent> ). The members of certificate groups, CA groups, intermediate-CA groups and schedule groups exist only in these child tables; the parent rows do not carry them. A child table the build does not serve is asked once, recorded as absent, and not asked again for the other parents. A path that changes the device on a GET is never read. docs.h: Predefined WPPs and the factory catalog
docs.x: Every FortiWeb ships the same predefined (factory) WPPs. SATOM keeps them in the Factory catalog , one entry per profile per firmware version, build number and REST API version: The first deep pass on a build reads the predefined WPPs in full and stores them. Later deep passes rebuild a predefined WPP from the catalog, without its sub-table reads, when the appliance's own rows for the profile and every object it names match the entry. Anything that does not match is read in full. An entry is read in full again once it is older than 7 days, and a profile whose entry is ambiguous is always read

With Also capture the CLI configuration (SSH, slow) on, SATOM opens one read-only SSH session and stores the output of show full-configuration in the configuration vault (see Backups ). The CLI-coverage report then compares the catalog against this box as swept. The pass can take up to 5 minutes; the line reads CLI capture (show full-configuration) running… up to 5 min . When the deep capture is also on, the CLI capture starts together with the deep pass and runs alongside it (one uses SSH, the other REST), so the sweep takes as long as the longer of the two instead of their sum. This is the one failure that ends a sweep immediately. On a FortiWeb, when an endpoint answers HTTP 401, SATOM asks the device's status once; on a FortiADC, SATOM logs in once more (an expired session is renewed and the read retried). If that is refused too, every further request would be another failed login, and the device locks the account after a few of them —

docs.x: Possible causes — The device refused every request: an expired or invalid licence (FortiWeb answers -20010 to every read), the host is down, or TLS fails. Solution — Read the example error. docs.x: Device health answers one question per appliance: is this device still there and in good shape? Each appliance gets a card with one badge — healthy , warning , critical or unknown — and every signal that is not healthy is written under the badge, so a state is never unexplained. The page reads only SATOM's own data; loading it never contacts an appliance.

Rolls four signals into one status per appliance. The worst signal wins, and unknown never counts as healthy: Signal (label on the card) ok warning critical unknown Harvest — the last five configuration harvests the latest one succeeded the latest failed (fewer than 3 in a row) 3 or more failed in a row never harvested Cache — age of the newest cached configuration younger than the cache budget (6 h by default) nothing cached, or older than the budget older than 4× the budget — Deep monitors — the device's enabled deep monitors all ok a probe warns or could not run, or all probes are disabled

Appliances registered under Appliances . Something that harvests them. A harvest is a full read of the device's configuration into SATOM's cache. It is written by: the scheduled action Sync device to local source of truth (or Sync device + push SoT off-box ); a Discovery / Rediscovery (recorded with trigger rediscovery ); SATOM itself after an approved change is written to a device. Deep monitors and capacity limits, if you want those two signals graded. See Deep monitors and Capacity limits .

On Tuesday its card reads critical : Harvest — harvest failing (5 runs in a row) - device refused the sweep (310 endpoints failed, 0 objects) — cache kept. First error: … Cache — cache 1 d old (budget 6 h) The configuration pages keep serving Monday's cache: a harvest in which the device returned nothing never overwrites the last good cache.

The page itself changes nothing. Scan hardware (SSH) stores one hardware record per appliance (CPU count and model, memory, disks, and the raw command output). The Architecture map reads the same record.

Possible causes — Nothing has been harvested, no deep monitors exist and no capacity caps are set. Unknown means "not measured", not "broken". Solution — Harvest the devices (see Understand "never harvested" hints above), configure deep monitors and capacity caps as needed. docs.h: "Deep monitors: N/M probes alerting" on a device that looks healthy
docs.x: Possible causes — Server-policy probes created before 2026-10-14 that point at VIPs SATOM cannot reach. Their result reads unreachable: ConnectTimeout or ConnectError , while CPU, memory and proxyd are ok. When the list is long, the line names four probes and adds "(+N more)". Solution — On Deep monitors , disable those probes, or make the VIPs routable from SATOM. Probes discovered from 2026-10-14 on are created disabled in this case. Verification — The card's deep-monitor line reads "N probes ok".

docs.h: "No deep monitors configured" on a device that was just added
docs.x: Possible causes — The device was added less than 3 minutes ago through a path that the next Collection sweep covers, or it is in maintenance. Solution — Wait for the next sweep or run Discover from device → Device baseline . A device in maintenance gets no probes until it leaves maintenance. Verification — The line changes to "N probes have never run", then to "N probes ok" after the first deep-monitor pass.

docs.h: "harvest failing (n runs in a row) - device refused the sweep (… endpoints failed, 0 objects) — cache kept."
docs.x: Possible causes — The device answered no request at all: down, licence-locked, wrong credentials, or a TLS failure. Solution — Run Test Connection on the appliance's page, then a Rediscovery to see per-endpoint errors.

Possible causes — Every deep monitor bound to the device is switched off. A disabled probe is reported as lost coverage, never as a passing check. Solution — Re-enable the monitors in Deep monitors , or remove them if the device no longer needs them.
Possible causes — No capacity catalog with a cap exists for this model and firmware. Solution — Set the hard max or operational cap under Capacity limits .
Possible causes — SSH is closed on the devices, or the credentials do not work over SSH. Solution — Check SSH from the Operator console .

docs.h: "no visible FortiWeb appliance to scan (the hardware scan is FortiWeb-only)"
docs.x: Possible causes — The current ADOM shows no FortiWeb appliance. The scan's command battery is written for FortiWeb only. Solution — Switch to the FortiWeb or Global ADOM. Other products show no hardware data on their cards.

Backing up SATOM itself (its database and data) is System backup .

docs.s: Keep the firmware images your appliances run — upgrade images and install media — in one checksummed library that the upgrade, boot-partition and provisioning flows pick from.

docs.x: The Firmware library stores firmware images on the SATOM node so that nobody has to upload a several-hundred-megabyte file for every device. Each image is recorded with its product, version, build, platform and a SHA-256 checksum. The appliance Upgrade and Boot Partition pages, the Upgrade Flow and Provisioning choose their images from here.

Uploads images with a live progress bar; the SHA-256 is then computed in the background and you are notified when the image is ready. Keeps two families of images apart: Upgrade ( .out ) — applied to a running appliance. Install — media to build a new machine ( .out , .zip , .qcow2 , .ova , .ovf , .vmdk , .img , .gz , .tgz ), optionally tagged with a hypervisor (KVM or VMware ESXi). Fills in Version and Build from a Fortinet filename (for example FWB_KVM-v7.6.8.M-build1128-FORTINET.out → 7.6.8, build 1128). A value you typed is never overwritten. Lists, downloads and deletes images. Deleting r
An administrator profile. The image file, at most the node's upload limit (the page states up to 600 MB ).

Every route of the library requires users.manage (administrators). 🔑 Permission — Without the permission The Firmware menu entry is part of the Administrator menu group, which is only drawn for administrators. The URLs answer 403 Forbidden . Operators still choose images on the appliance Upgrade page; they only cannot add or remove them. The menu entry exists in the FortiWeb and FortiAnalyzer ADOMs. The page also opens in the FortiADC ADOM by URL.

docs.h: The image does not appear on an appliance's Upgrade page
docs.x: Possible causes - The image's Product differs from the appliance's kind. - The image's Platform is Hardware and the appliance is a VM (or the other way round). - The image's Type is Install . Install media builds a new machine and is not a flash payload; only Upgrade images are offered. - You uploaded in another ADOM; product ADOMs only see their own product. Solution — Check product, type and platform in the Stored firmware table.

Advanced Integrity The checksum recorded at upload is checked again every time an image is read for a flash. A file that changed on disk is refused ( sha256 mismatch … recorded …, file … ) before anything is sent to a device. Advanced How the upload survives navigation The page sends the file in a single upload request. It keeps running when you change pages because navigation in SATOM does not unload the page. Advanced ADOM rule on upload The ADOM of the request decides the product, not the form. A hand-crafted upload in the FortiADC ADOM is always filed as a FortiADC image.

docs.s: Plan a firmware maintenance window for many appliances as one staged workflow — bulk pre-upgrade evidence, one change request, a scheduled rollout in rounds, and live execution progress.

docs.x: The Upgrade Flow treats a firmware maintenance window as one workflow instead of a per-appliance chore. On one page you pre-flight every appliance in the window, raise one change request that cites all of that evidence, plan how many appliances go down at a time, and then watch execution appliance by appliance. The page owns no workflow of its own: the pre-flight is the same one the per-appliance Upgrade Preparation page runs, and the change request is created through the same path as Change Requests .

The page is organised in numbered stages: 1 Pre-upgrade (bulk) Choose the destination version, tick appliances, run a read-only pre-flight on each; one stored run per appliance 2 Change request (CRQ) Raise ONE change of type upgrade citing the runs you choose — or split the selection into waves 3 The change itself The raised change is shown in full on the same page: approve, schedule, notify, export, read the document 4 Scheduled rollout Decide how many appliances per round and the gap; saved as real scheduled tasks once approved 5 Execution Per-appliance progress page, polled live, with a Sta

The page says so: This flow covers fortiweb: the products whose firmware SATOM can flash from a change. FortiADC has no flash path, so its pre-upgrade runs from the appliance page only. Uses the same form and the same creation rules as Change Requests → New, with three differences: the change type is fixed to the upgrade type, the affected devices are the ones ticked in stage 1 (read-only here), and you come back to the flow afterwards. docs.s: Stage 4 of the Upgrade Flow — plan how many appliances go down per round, save the rollout as scheduled tasks once the change is approved, and follow execution appliance by appliance.

docs.x: Once the change request for a window exists, card 4 — Scheduled rollout decides how many of its appliances go down at a time. Each round becomes a real one-shot task on Automations (and on the Calendar ) bound to the change, and is re-checked against the change's approval and window when it fires. The Execution page shows per-appliance progress while the rounds run.

Splits the change's appliances into rounds of at most N appliances, a fixed number of minutes apart, starting at the window start. Before approval, saves the plan on the change without creating any task. When the change is approved, the plan is turned into scheduled tasks automatically. After approval, creates or updates the scheduled tasks directly. Shows the saved rounds (start time, appliances, state). On the execution page, polls progress every 5 seconds and offers Start now inside an approved window.

⚠️ Warning — No firmware is flashed by the scheduled upgrade The automated firmware-upgrade executor is a guarded placeholder in this release. When a round fires inside its window, every appliance is graded failed with the summary "Firmware upgrade for <appliance> is not executed by the headless service layer (no upgrade runbook); no firmware was flashed." , and the change request then closes as failed . Use the rollout to plan and document the window; perform the flash per appliance from the Firmware page, which requires its own approved, open change request.

All rounds of a rollout are bound to the same change request. A round that succeeds and is not the last leaves the change in progress for the next round; only the last round closes it, as completed when it succeeded. A round that fails closes the change as failed at once, so the remaining rounds are refused at fire time ( "change request: change request is failed" ) instead of flashing on. ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: a rollout split into rounds is no longer closed by its first round, and the Schedule button on the change request now honours the rollout plan saved on the change. docs.s: Check whether an appliance's whole configuration survives a move to a target firmware build — what blocks, what is renamed, what changes behind your back — before the upgrade window.

docs.x: The Migration report checks every object and field an appliance holds today against what SATOM knows about a target firmware build , and gives one verdict: ready, ready with warnings, blocked, or cannot assess. It answers the question every upgrade window starts with — what of this box's configuration does the new build reject, rename or change? — before the image is uploaded.

Reads the appliance's newest show full-configuration backup (or one you choose) in memory and compares it with the target build's CLI schema in the API library . Classifies each finding: Class Examples block an object or field the box uses is gone in the target; an enum value the target no longer accepts; a value out of range; a type the value does not fit translate a rename covered by an operator rename map warn a probable rename (same CLI attribute id, not mapped yet); a default that changed under a field left at its default; no evidence for the object on the target; a target not completely

At least one configuration backup of the appliance in the vault (a show full-configuration dump). Without one the verdict is cannot assess . The target build has a CLI schema in the library — harvested ( Schema builds ) or imported from a knowledge pack. A FortiWeb, FortiADC or FortiGate appliance. (A FortiGate has no stored configuration backup yet, so it reads cannot assess .)

docs.s: Build a new appliance machine step by step (address, DNS name, virtual machine, power-on, registration) as a recorded run that can be preflighted and rolled back.

docs.x: Device Provisioning builds an appliance that does not exist yet. Each build is a run : SATOM reserves a management address, publishes a DNS name, creates and powers on a virtual machine on a registered hypervisor, checks that the address answers, and registers the result as an appliance. Every step is written to the run log, so a half-finished run can be rolled back from what it recorded. It is the counterpart of System Provisioning , which pushes system configuration to appliances that already exist.

Offers five modes that decide how much of the pipeline a run performs (see Modes ). Preflight asks the hypervisor what it can actually do and lists blockers and warnings before anything changes. Run walks the mode's plan; a run refuses to start when preflight reports a blocker. Roll back undoes, in reverse, only what the run recorded creating: the virtual machine, the DNS record and an IPAM-allocated address. Runs are scoped to the ADOM they were created in. A run started in the FortiADC ADOM is invisible from the FortiWeb ADOM, and opening its URL there returns 404 Not Found . 1 Create run na

For every mode except Config only : at least one enabled hypervisor registered by an administrator in Settings › Hypervisors (Proxmox or ESXi). Disabled hypervisors are not offered. Optional: an install image uploaded on the Firmware page as an install image. Upgrade images are a separate list and are not offered. Optional: an IPAM backend and a DNS backend in Settings › DNS Records, if you want SATOM to allocate the address or publish the hostname. ℹ️ Note — No hypervisor registered With no enabled hypervisor the page shows "No hypervisor is registered" and the Mode list offers only Config on

Action Gate in code Granular key that is meant Open the page, the run detail and the run list operations.view operations.view Create a run, Preflight , Run / Resume , Roll back coarse config_write operations.apply The Automation menu group, and therefore the Device Provisioning entry, is drawn only for users whose profile grants config_write . That coarse key is unlocked by any of operations.apply , operations.template_save , operations.template_apply , operations.template_approve , protection.edit , protection.apply , network.edit , network.apply , appliances.edit or appliances.apply , so the

Open Automation → Device Provisioning . Click New machine . The New machine form opens. Fill in the fields (see Configuration ). Machine name is required. In the Global ADOM, pick the Product . In a product ADOM the product is that ADOM and cannot be changed. Click Create run . The form answers "Run created. Press Preflight to see what it will be able to do before anything changes." and the run appears in Runs with status draft .

In Runs , click Preflight on the run. Read the result under the form: - Plan: the steps this mode will perform, in order. - Blocked: reasons the run cannot finish. Run will be refused. - Warnings: things that will need a manual action. - "Nothing blocks this run." when there is neither. - "Preflight did not run:" followed by the reason when the server refused the request or failed. That is not a verdict on the run. Preflight only reads the hypervisor's capabilities. It changes nothing and can be pressed at any time. Modes that do not touch a hypervisor ( Config only ) always pass.

Click Run . SATOM repeats the preflight check first; when it finds a blocker the run is refused with "preflight refused this run" and the blockers are listed. Otherwise the planned steps execute one after another in that single press, until the plan ends, a step fails, or the mode stops by design. Watch Step , Progress and Status in the Runs table. Click the run name to open its detail page. Status Meaning What to do draft Created, nothing run yet. Preflight, then Run. running Steps are executing. Wait. paused The mode stopped where it is designed to stop. The reason is shown. Read the reason.

Click a run name. The detail page shows: the mode, current step, status and address; the current error or pause reason (yellow when paused, red otherwise); Pipeline : every step of the pipeline as a badge. Greyed steps are not part of this mode's plan — "they are skipped by design, not failures." ; Run log : one row per step attempt and rollback action ( Step , OK , Detail , At ), newest first. The detail page has no action buttons; use the Runs table.

In Runs , click Roll back . The button changes to Confirm roll back for four seconds. Click Confirm roll back . The run becomes aborted . Its log lists what was removed. ⚠️ Warning — Roll back is offered on finished runs too Roll back is shown for every run that is not already aborted , including done runs. On a done run it still deletes the virtual machine SATOM created, the DNS record it published and the address it allocated from IPAM.

The plan of each mode is fixed in code. A step not in the plan is skipped. Creating, running and rolling back a run each write an audit log entry ( provision.device.create , provision.device.advance , provision.device.rollback ). Preflight is not audited. docs.x: Possible causes - Resume continues the Semi run with reachable , which probes the management address of the run. The first-boot dialog was not completed yet, or it set a different address. Solution 1. Finish the first-boot dialog on the hypervisor console, with the management address and admin password entered on the run. 2. Press Run . The run retries reachable , then registers the appliance. Verification - The run ends done and the appliance appears in Appliances .

docs.h: "Preflight did not run: HTTP 403 …" or the Runs table shows "read-only"
docs.x: Possible causes - Your profile does not grant config_write , so the server refuses Preflight, Run and Roll back. Solution 1. Ask an administrator for operations.apply (see Users and profiles ). Verification - The Automation group appears in your menu, New machine is shown, and Preflight lists a Plan: .

Possible causes - "hypervisor target is gone — the machine … must be removed by hand" . - "could not delete the machine: …" , "could not remove the DNS record: …" or "could not release the address: …" . Solution 1. Read the run's error and its Run log rows starting with rollback: . 2. Remove the named items by hand on the hypervisor, DNS or IPAM system. Verification - The external system no longer holds the machine, record or address.

Advanced Where things are stored Runs are kept in the provision_runs table; hypervisors in hypervisor_targets . Both are created automatically at start-up. The admin password and hypervisor secrets are stored encrypted. Each run keeps the last 200 log entries; each entry's detail is cut at 2,000 characters. The page lists the 50 most recent runs of the current ADOM. The same list is available as JSON at /device-provisioning/data ( scope , runs , has_hypervisor ).
