docs.x: System Provisioning pushes system-level configuration to FortiWeb appliances that already exist. You compose a system profile — an ordered list of configuration objects with the values to write — save it as a versioned template, have it approved, then preview it and push it to selected appliances or to the whole fleet with a canary first. The same area holds Combos (called baselines in links and URLs): one combo per zone × line × department permutation, each carrying approved templates and applying them to the appliances classified into that scope. To build a machine that does not exist yet, u

Profiles : author, edit (each save is a new version), approve or reject, delete, and Preview & deploy an approved profile. Element picker offers every FortiWeb configuration ( cmdb ) object known to the endpoint registry, grouped by GUI section, plus a curated set of system elements (global settings / hostname, DNS, NTP, FortiGuard, interfaces, static routes, SNMP, RADIUS, LDAP, user groups, admin access profiles, administrators, syslog, FortiAnalyzer). Secret hygiene : secret-looking fields (passwords, shared secrets, keys) are removed from sensitive elements before the profile is saved, and

The FortiWeb ADOM. System Provisioning composes FortiWeb objects only; the menu entry is shown only in the FortiWeb ADOM, and the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs redirect to their home page if the URL is opened there. Opening it from the Global ADOM switches that tab to the FortiWeb ADOM. The endpoint registry must be loaded, otherwise the element picker is empty ( "No configuration objects are available from the registry yet. Load the registry / connect an appliance, then reload this page." ). Registered FortiWeb appliances to apply to. For combos and profile scopes: zone

Leave it unticked for collections. - mkey (optional) : for a collection, the key of an existing object to update. Empty creates a new object. - Values : the field

Click Edit (pencil) on the profile. Change the elements or scope and click Save profile . Saving always creates a new version (v2, v3 …) with status Pending ; the previous version is kept. docs.h: "Could not save profile: Profile name is required"
docs.x: Possible causes - Name was empty. Solution 1. Enter a name and click Save profile . Your rows are kept on the form. Verification - The profile appears in the list as Pending .

docs.h: "Could not save profile: Add at least one provisioning element"
docs.x: Possible causes - Every row has Element left on — select a configuration object — . Solution 1. Pick an element in at least one row. Verification - System profile " " saved (v ).

docs.h: "Could not save profile: Element ' ': values are not valid JSON (…)"
docs.x: Possible causes - The Values box is not valid JSON (missing quotes, trailing comma). - A similar message "values must be a JSON object" means the JSON is a list or a single value. Solution 1. Correct the JSON so it is one object: { "field": "value" } . Verification - The profile saves.

docs.h: "Could not save profile: Unknown provisioning element: "
docs.x: Possible causes - The element no longer exists in the endpoint registry (shown in the picker as (not in registry) ). Solution 1. Choose another element or remove the row. Verification - The profile saves.

Possible causes - The newest version is Pending or Rejected . Editing an approved profile creates a new pending version. Solution 1. Have an administrator approve the newest version. Verification - The rocket button appears on the row.
Possible causes - One of the two fields was empty. Solution 1. Open Preview & deploy again and fill in both. Verification - The preview page opens.

docs.h: "Select at least one appliance, or choose "Entire fleet"."
docs.x: Possible causes - Selected appliances was chosen with nothing selected. SATOM refuses rather than treating an empty selection as the fleet. Solution 1. Select appliances, or choose Entire fleet (all appliances) explicitly. Verification - The preview lists the intended appliances.

docs.h: "Aborted. The canary device failed — the remaining devices were skipped."
docs.x: Possible causes - A request failed on the first appliance; the failing row shows the error. Solution 1. Fix the profile values (or the appliance), save, get the new version approved, and deploy again. Verification - The canary block shows OK .

docs.h: A secret field was not written
docs.x: Possible causes - Saving removes secret-looking fields from sensitive elements, and a deployment does not send them. The preview names the affected elements. Solution 1. Set the secret on the appliance directly, or through a tool that sends it. Verification - Check the object on the appliance.

docs.h: "… is pending: only an approved system profile can be deployed live."
docs.x: Possible causes - Confirm & apply to live devices was sent for a version that is Pending or Rejected (for example a preview opened before a new version was saved). The refusal is recorded in the audit log; nothing was written. Solution 1. Have an administrator approve the version, then deploy again. Verification - The result page shows the Canary block.

Possible causes - The template is locked (its delete button is disabled) or was already deleted. Solution 1. A locked profile (lock icon next to its name) cannot be deleted from this page. Reload the list to check whether it was already removed. Verification - The row is gone, or shows the lock icon.

docs.h: "Deploy of " " refused — : no value for . Set the values on the device bindings, then apply."
docs.x: The same cause shows on a combo as Baseline rollout "<name>" refused — … . Possible causes - The profile (or a template of the combo) has a {{ variable }} placeholder, and the named device's binding gives it no value. Solution 1. Open the template in the Template Library and, under Devices this template governs , set the variable in the device's Variables (JSON) . 2. Preview again. Verification - The preview no longer shows The live deploy will be refused: … .

docs.h: "Baseline " " matches no devices for its scope."
docs.x: Possible causes - No appliance has the combo's zone, line and department. Solution 1. Classify appliances (see Classification ). Verification - The combo card shows a non-zero Matching devices count.

Possible causes - Nothing is assigned to the combo, or the assigned templates contain no elements. Solution 1. Assign the templates to push via Assign on the combo page or the Combos page. Verification - The apply preview lists requests.

docs.h: "All combos already exist — nothing to generate."
docs.x: Possible causes - Every permutation already has a combo. Solution 1. Add zones, lines or departments in Classification first if you expected new combos. Verification - Generate missing combos shows a count.

docs.h: "Could not assign: Template " " is not approved"
docs.x: Possible causes - The template is pending or rejected. Solution 1. Approve it, then assign again. Verification - Template assigned to combo.

Advanced How profiles are stored A profile is a template of kind system-profile with a body of line , _scope (zone, line, department) and items (key, endpoint, data, singleton, mkey, label, sensitive). An element is sensitive when the curated catalog says so (SNMP v3 users, RADIUS, LDAP, administrators) or its name contains words such as password , secret , radius , ldap , admin . For sensitive elements, any field whose name contains password , passwd , pwd , secret , psk , passphrase , private-key , privkey or credential is removed recursively before saving. Approval is per version: approving

docs.s: Run FortiOS CLI commands on an appliance over SSH, test a username and password against a device, and package the session for Fortinet TAC — plus the read-only SSH Console on each appliance page.

docs.x: SATOM has two consoles that open an SSH session to an appliance: The Device Console (Administrator or Automation → Device Console) is the one place in SATOM where SSH can change an appliance. You paste a script of CLI commands, SATOM runs it in one session and shows the answer to every line. The same page can test a single username and password against a FortiOS device, and build a redacted support bundle for a Fortinet TAC ticket. The SSH Console on an appliance's page ( Console button) is read-only : it accepts only get , show and diagnose commands, one at a time, and refuses a diagnose comm

Device Console ( /console/ ) Runs up to 200 commands, one per line, in one SSH session, so config / edit / end blocks work as they do on the box. Classifies every line before anything is sent: forbidden — execute factoryreset , execute formatlogdisk , execute erase-disk , disk/USB-disk format . Refused at every permission level. disruptive — execute reboot , execute shutdown , execute restore , execute ha … , execute backup|migrate … tftp|ftp , set password / set passwd (and unset of them). Sent only after you tick the acknowledgement and type the appliance name. safe — everything else. Reads

The appliance is registered in Appliances with an SSH port (default 22) and the admin credential SATOM uses. SATOM reuses that credential for SSH. The SSH Console on an appliance page is offered for FortiWeb and FortiADC appliances only. Other kinds get the flash "This action is not available for this appliance kind." On a multi-ADOM FortiWeb registered as several rows, the SSH Console belongs to the chassis' device row (see The two consoles compared ).

Action Required permission Open the Device Console, Run , Build bundle the legacy config_write gate. Any one of these granular keys grants it: appliances.apply , appliances.edit , protection.edit , protection.apply , network.edit , network.apply , operations.apply , operations.template_save , operations.template_apply , operations.template_approve Test login (credential test) users.manage Open the SSH Console on an appliance appliances.view Run in the SSH Console on an appliance appliances.apply Without config_write , /console/ answers 403 . The Device Console menu entry is drawn only for user

docs.h: Run commands in the Device Console
docs.x: Open Administrator → Device Console (administrators) or Automation → Device Console (other users). In Appliance , pick a device ( — pick one — ). The list shows the appliances of the active ADOM; in the Global ADOM it shows every product. Type or paste the script in Commands — one per line, up to 200 . Lines starting with # are comments. Optional: use Insert a read-only preset to append a preset command to the script. Only the presets of the picked appliance's product are offered (FortiWeb or FortiADC); FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator have none. Leave Stop at the first failed command tick

Run a script (the bundle form appears under the result once a transcript exists). In Send to Fortinet TAC , optionally enter the TAC ticket number (optional) and What you were trying to do (optional) . Keep Attach the read-only diagnostic battery ticked to add the product's diagnostic commands (SATOM opens a second session for them). For a FortiAnalyzer or FortiAuthenticator SATOM has no battery; the bundle then holds the transcript and a DIAGNOSTICS-MISSING.txt saying so. Press Build bundle . The browser downloads tac-<appliance>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tar.gz (UTC time stamp).

In Test a credential , enter Host or IP , SSH port (default 22), Username and Password . Press Test login . Read the badges: reachable / unreachable , authenticated / not authenticated , can read / read not confirmed , and the time taken. If the login worked, the firmware ( Firmware ) and Device hostname from get system status are shown. Write-access hint (raw) shows what the box answered when the session tried to set the CLI pager. It is evidence, not a verdict: a box that refused it for another reason looks the same as a read-only account. The device does not need to be registered in SATOM.

docs.h: Use the read-only SSH Console on an appliance
docs.x: Open Appliances , then the appliance. In Appliance Actions , press Console (on the Appliances list, the terminal icon does the same for FortiWeb and FortiADC rows). Both are shown only with appliances.apply . Click a preset in Presets , or type a command after $ and press Run (or Enter). The output appears below. Errors are shown as ERROR: <reason> .

🧪 Example — Change the DNS server on one appliance Script in the Device Console, appliance fweb-01 : # point the box at the new resolver config system dns set primary 192.0.2.53 end get system dns All four lines are safe , so no acknowledgement is needed. The three configuration lines return no output ( no output — normal for a configuration command that succeeded ); get system dns shows the new value. If config system dns had failed, the script would stop there and the set line would be marked not_run instead of landing at the top level of the CLI.

Each Run and Test login , each Build bundle , and each SSH Console command that completes is written to the Audit log . console.run records the appliance, the commands (redacted), their tiers, whether a disruptive acknowledgement was given, the stop-on-error setting and the failure count. console.verify_credentials records host, username and port, the three results and any error — never the password. Run , Test login and SSH Console commands are device actions: one that takes longer than the inline window (about two seconds by default) continues as a background job in the Jobs dock. Build bund

Possible causes - The script is empty or contains only # comment lines. Solution 1. Enter at least one command that does not start with # . Verification - The result header shows 1 cmd or more.

docs.h: "This script contains a disruptive command. Tick the acknowledgement and type the appliance name exactly (…) to send it."
docs.x: Possible causes - The script contains a reboot, shutdown, restore, HA, clear-text backup/migrate or password command — written in full or abbreviated ( exe reb , set passw ) — and the checkbox is not ticked or the typed name differs from the appliance name (it is compared exactly). The disruptive row itself reads refused: … Tick 'I understand this script is disruptive' and type the appliance name to send it. Solution 1. Tick I understand this script is disruptive . 2. Type the appliance name exactly as shown in the flash message. 3. Press Run again. Verification - The rows show ok / error inst

docs.h: "refused: … This command has no path through SATOM at any permission level"
docs.x: Possible causes - A line matched the forbidden tier (factory reset, format log disk, erase disk, disk format). The match is made anywhere in the unquoted part of the line, so a line pasted from a session log such as FortiWeb # execute factoryreset is still recognised. - The line is an abbreviation of a forbidden command: exe fa , exe factoryres or exec format are read exactly like the full words, because the device CLI runs them that way. Solution 1. Remove the line. If you really need it, run it from the appliance's own console. 2. A value that merely mentions such a command must be quoted wi

docs.h: All rows show "the session never opened"
docs.x: Possible causes - The appliance is unreachable on its SSH port, the stored credential is wrong, or the stored host key does not match. Solution 1. Use Test a credential with the same host and port to tell unreachable apart from not authenticated . 2. Correct the host, SSH port or credential on the appliance in Appliances . Verification - Test login shows reachable and authenticated , and a new Run returns output.

docs.h: "… the appliance host is a retired placeholder (…), so nothing was sent"
docs.x: Possible causes - The appliance's host ends in .invalid (marked · retired in the picker). SATOM does not dial it. Solution 1. Pick the live appliance, or update the host in Appliances if the device is back in service. Verification - The picker entry no longer shows · retired .

docs.h: "12 credential checks in 300s is the limit for one operator — try again in …s."
docs.x: Possible causes - More than 12 credential tests by the same user within 5 minutes. Solution 1. Wait the number of seconds shown and test again. The tool tests one credential you already have; it is not meant to search for one. Verification - Test login returns badges instead of the error.

docs.h: "the credential was accepted but 'get system status' returned nothing usable …"
docs.x: Possible causes - The account logs in but its admin profile has no read access. Solution 1. Give the account an admin profile with read access on the device, then test again. Verification - The can read badge turns green and Firmware is shown.

docs.h: "'…' is not a read-only command — only diag, diagnose, get, show are allowed in the console"
docs.x: Possible causes - A command other than get / show / diagnose / diag was typed in the SSH Console on an appliance page. Each statement separated by ; , & or | is checked. Solution 1. Use a read command, or use the Device Console if you need to change the device (requires config_write ). Verification - The output shows the command's answer instead of ERROR: .

Possible causes - A diagnose command typed in the SSH Console contains a word that changes the device, for example diagnose debug kernel sysrq command crash or diagnose sys kill … . An abbreviation reads as the full word: the message then says 'kil' reads as 'kill', which changes the device state . Solution 1. Use a read-only diagnose command. A command that must change the device belongs in the Device Console , with its acknowledgement gates. Verification - The output shows the command's answer instead of ERROR: .

docs.h: The SSH Console sends you to another appliance row
docs.x: Possible causes - You opened the console on an ADOM row of a multi-ADOM FortiWeb; the console belongs to the chassis' device row. Solution 1. Use the device row named in the flash message. Verification - The page title reads Console — .

A Process step is stricter: a disruptive step must name the one appliance it may disrupt. The read-only SSH Console uses a separate allowlist ( get , show , diagnose , diag ) that other read-only SSH features also rely on; the Device Console does not relax it. docs.k: docker container compose agent restart update release proxy certificate nginx stack docker operations operations agent satom-docker container update restart container users.manage
docs.s: On a Docker installation of SATOM, restart a service of the stack, switch the node to another release and install the proxy certificate — all through the optional operations agent.

docs.x: Container operations is the administration page for a SATOM node that runs as a Docker stack. It is the container counterpart of Software Update , the Services card in Settings and the node certificate in Node TLS . The page itself never touches Docker: every button only queues a request , and a separate, optional container — the operations agent — re-checks the request against a closed list and does the work.

Shows the state of the Operations agent (live, not answering, not enabled), its version and the stack's version. Lists which host-only Capabilities the agent currently performs for this node. Services of this stack — start, stop or restart the allowed services. Update — switch this node to another SATOM release ( X.Y.Z ), with automatic rollback if the console does not come back healthy. Proxy certificate — install a certificate and private key into the TLS proxy and reload it. Recent agent requests — the last 15 requests with their steps and result. On a host (non-container) installation the

SATOM runs in the container runtime . The menu entry only appears there. For any action, the operations agent must be enabled and live (it reported a heartbeat within the last 60 seconds). Without it the page opens, explains why, and offers nothing. Update additionally needs the installer layout (a node set up with the installer, not a manual checkout). ⚠️ Warning — The agent is root on the host The agent mounts the Docker socket: whoever controls it is root on the host. It is therefore optional and off unless you enable it (run the installer again and answer yes to the operations agent, or se

Every route of this page — the page, its status polling, and each action — requires users.manage ( Administrator ). Without it the page answers 403 , and the menu entry is not shown (the whole Administrator group is drawn only for users.manage ). Where it is reachable. The menu entry is in the Global ADOM's Administrator group. The page also opens in the FortiWeb ADOM by URL; in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs it redirects to that ADOM's home page.

Badge Meaning live The agent reported within the last 60 s. The card shows Last heartbeat , Agent version , stack version and Layout ( installer or manual ). not answering The agent is enabled but silent (or has never reported). The card shows the reason and "Nothing is queued while the agent is silent. On the host:" satom-docker ps agent · satom-docker logs agent . not enabled The stack runs without the agent. The card explains how to enable it. Under live you may see agent and stack differ — an update recreates every service except the agent, so run satom-docker up -d on the host to bring it

docs.h: Restart, stop or start a service
docs.x: In Services of this stack , find the service. Press one of the buttons in Actions ( restart , stop or start , depending on the service and its state). Confirm the browser prompt ( <action> <service>? ). The page follows the request and reloads when it finishes, with the request highlighted in Recent agent requests . Service Label Actions allowed web Web application restart only scheduler Scheduler start, stop, restart cron Periodic jobs start, stop, restart proxy TLS proxy (nginx) restart only postgres PostgreSQL restart only redis Redis (rate limits) restart only victoria-metrics Metrics stor

In Update , check the running version ( The stack runs … ) and the releases Already on this host ( tree only = the source is present but not the image). Type the version, e.g. 2.3.1 . Type UPDATE in the confirmation box. Press Update this node . Wait: the console restarts during the update; the page keeps polling and reloads when the request finishes. On a primary + standby pair, update the primary first (schema changes can only be applied on the writable primary), then the standby. Releases without the operations agent are refused here; switch to them with satom-setup.sh on the host.

In Proxy certificate , choose Certificate (PEM) , Private key (PEM) and optionally Chain (optional) . Press Install and reload the proxy . The result appears next to the button: installed: · days , or the reason for the refusal.

Field Description Required Example Version Target release, X.Y.Z (a leading v is ignored) Yes (update) 2.3.1 type UPDATE Typed confirmation; must be exactly UPDATE Yes (update) UPDATE Certificate (PEM) Server certificate file Yes (certificate) server.crt Private key (PEM) Matching private key Yes (certificate) server.key Chain (optional) Intermediate chain No chain.pem The update and certificate controls are disabled when the agent is not live; the update controls are also disabled on a manual layout.

🧪 Example — Recover the scheduler on a Docker node Scheduled actions stopped firing. On Container operations the agent is live and the Scheduler row shows a red badge. Press restart , confirm restart scheduler? , and wait. The page reloads with a ctr-restart request for scheduler · restart in Recent agent requests , state success , and the Scheduler badge is green again.

Each action writes a status row (state queued ) and a request file that the agent picks up. Recent agent requests shows Request id, Kind ( ctr-restart , ctr-update , ctr-cert ), Target , By , State ( success , failed , or in yellow queued / running ) and a Log of every step with ✓ or ✗. After a start or restart the agent waits up to 3 minutes for the service to be running and healthy. An update downloads the release if it is not on the host, loads the image the release publishes (checked against its checksum and its version; built on the host only when the release publishes none), recreates ev

Possible causes - The confirmation box does not contain exactly UPDATE . Solution 1. Type UPDATE (upper case) and press Update this node again. Verification - A new ctr-update row appears in Recent agent requests .
Possible causes - The version is empty or not three numbers separated by dots. Solution 1. Enter a version such as 2.3.1 . Verification - The request is queued instead of refused.

docs.h: "The operations agent is enabled but not answering (…)"
docs.x: Possible causes - The agent container is stopped or its heartbeat is older than 60 seconds, or its time stamp is in the future (clock problem). Solution 1. On the host, run satom-docker ps agent and satom-docker logs agent . 2. Recreate it with satom-docker up -d . Verification - The agent badge shows live and the capabilities show via agent .

docs.h: "… is not allowed on '…' from this console"
docs.x: Possible causes - The action is not in the service's allowed list (for example a stop on web , proxy or postgres ), or the service is the agent or tls-init . Solution 1. Use an allowed action from the table above, or act on the host with satom-docker . Verification - The button offered on the page is accepted.

docs.x: Possible causes - The certificate or the key file was not selected. Solution 1. Select both Certificate (PEM) and Private key (PEM) and try again. Verification - The result reads installed: … .

docs.h: A request ended "failed" with "request expired: queued … s ago (limit 600 s)"
docs.x: Possible causes - The agent picked the request up more than 10 minutes after it was queued. It does not run a restart or an update late. Solution 1. Check that the agent is live, then send the request again. Verification - The new request reaches success .

docs.h: An update ended "failed" with "the update did not come up healthy; rolled back"
docs.x: Possible causes - The web service did not become healthy within 7 minutes on the new release. Solution 1. Read the steps in the Log column of the request. 2. Fix the cause on the host before trying again. Verification - The stack version in the agent card is the release you expect.

Advanced How requests travel The web container has no Docker socket. A request is a JSON file in the node's update-request queue plus a status file; both directories are volumes shared with the agent. The allowlist of services and actions exists twice — in the web application, so the page only offers what the agent accepts, and in the agent itself, which is the security boundary and re-validates every request. Nothing is queued while the agent is silent, so nothing fires later by surprise. Advanced Runtime detection The container runtime is selected only when the environment variable SATOM_RUN

docs.s: The installation-wide list of named networks a new server policy puts its VIP on. Each segment holds one or more networks (CIDR, gateway, optional interface) tried in order when IPAM assigns the address, and is scoped to a zone, line and departments.
docs.x: ℹ️ Note New: a segment holds one or more networks . When the VIP is reserved from IPAM it is taken from the first network with a free address, then the next — the operator no longer picks which. See Several networks in one segment .

Network Segments is the registry of the networks new server policies put their VIP on. Each segment has a name, one or more networks (a CIDR and its gateway, optionally the appliance interface that reaches it), a default interface , and can be scoped to a zone , a line and one or more departments from the Classification catalogs. When a new server policy is built from a line, the wizard reserves (or checks) the VIP in the networks of the segment that line receives and binds the VIP to that network's interface.

Keeps one list of segments for the whole SATOM installation (it is not per ADOM). Validates every CIDR, refuses two segments with the same name and refuses the same CIDR twice in one segment. Gives the new-policy wizard the networks to reserve the VIP from, in order, and the interface to put it on. Feeds the segment choice of a line: Line profiles name segments explicitly; without a profile, SATOM falls back to the segments whose Line equals the line name. Lets other pages group appliances by segment: an appliance belongs to the segment one of whose networks contains its management address (us

Zones, lines and departments are defined on the Classification page. The segment form offers them as choices; a blank value means any . Nothing needs to be registered on an appliance first — segments are SATOM data, not device configuration.

All routes require users.manage ( Administrator ). Without it, /segments/ answers 403 and the menu entry is not shown (the Administrator menu group is drawn only for users.manage ). Where it is reachable. ADOM Behaviour FortiWeb Administrator → Network Segments FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator Administrator → Network Segments Global No menu entry; opening the URL switches the tab to the FortiWeb ADOM FortiADC Not reachable; the URL redirects to the FortiADC home page The page is also linked from the Line Profiles page ( Network segments button).

Open Administrator → Network Segments . Check the Classification reference card for the zones, lines and departments available. To change them, press Edit catalogs . Press Add segment to add an empty row, or edit an existing row in place. Fill in Name , the Interface (pre-filled port1 on a new row; used by every network that does not name its own) and an optional Note . Under Networks , fill in the CIDR and gateway of the first network. Press Add network for each further one, and leave its interface blank unless that network is reached through another port. The order shown is the order address

When the line's segment has more than one network: IPAM reserves the VIP (wizard option Reserve the VIP from IPAM ): the address comes from the first network with a free address . If IPAM refuses one — full, or any other error — the next is tried. The address step of the run names every network that refused and why, and the preview shows the order ( would take the next free address from A, then B if it has none free ). A network no IPAM backend can serve (no backend claims it, a tie, an unreachable backend) is shown as a warning, this network will NOT be tried . The plan blocks only when no ne

Press the trash button at the end of the row. The row disappears from the form. Press Save Segments . The saved list is exactly what the form holds. ⚠️ Warning — Removing a segment a line still needs A Line profile that names a segment you deleted reports "segment ' ' is named by this line but no longer exists in Network segments" , and the new-policy wizard treats it as a problem rather than a shorter list.

Field Description Required Example Name Identifies the network. Must be unique (exact, case-sensitive comparison). Line profiles refer to segments by this name. Yes, unless only a CIDR is given web-dmz Zone Classification zone the segment belongs to; — any — = no restriction No dmz Line Classification line; used to infer segments for a line that has no line profile No public-web Departments Any number of classification departments No sales , support Networks → CIDR Network in CIDR notation, IPv4 or IPv6; host bits are allowed and the value is stored as typed. One row per network, in allocation

🧪 Example — Two departments on one network Sales and Support both publish services from 198.51.100.0/24 , reached through port3 . Name Zone Line Departments Networks Interface shared-apps internal intranet sales , support 198.51.100.0/24 gw 198.51.100.1 port3 Create one row and select both departments. A second row named shared-apps would be refused on save. 🧪 Example — A segment that grows a second network web-dmz started as {ip}/24 on port3 and is nearly full. Add a second network {ip}/24 , gateway {ip} , interface port9 . New policies keep taking addresses from {ip}/24 while it has any; aft

The list is saved as a whole and the page shows " network segment(s) saved." The Audit log records segments.save with the number of segments. Line plans, the new-policy wizard, the Analysis dashboard and appliance grouping use the new list immediately. Renaming or removing a zone, line or department on the Classification page updates the segments that use it; removing a value still used by segments asks you to decide what happens to them first.

docs.h: "two or more segments share the name(s) '…' — a segment name identifies one network, so add the extra department to the existing row instead of adding a second row."
docs.x: Possible causes - Two rows carry the same name. Solution 1. Merge the rows: keep one, select all its departments, delete the other. 2. Or give the second network a different name. 3. Press Save Segments . Verification - The success message appears. Nothing was written by the refused save — the previous list is still in place, so re-enter the edits you made.

Possible causes - A CIDR is not a valid IPv4/IPv6 network (for example 192.0.2.0/33 ). Solution 1. Only the networks with an invalid CIDR were dropped; the segment and its other networks were saved. Add the network again with a valid CIDR. 2. Press Save Segments . Verification - The network is present after reload and the warning does not appear.

docs.h: "a segment lists the same network twice (…) — keep one entry per CIDR."
docs.x: Possible causes - Two networks of one segment carry the same CIDR. Solution 1. Remove one of them (keep the one with the right gateway) and press Save Segments . Nothing was written by the refused save.

docs.h: A line gets no segments, or the wrong ones
docs.x: Possible causes - The line has no line profile and no segment's Line equals the line name exactly. - The line profile names a segment that was renamed or deleted. Solution 1. Declare the line's segments on Line profiles , or set the Line of the right segments here. Verification - The line profile shows its segments without a missing segment problem.

Advanced Storage and parsing Segments are stored as one JSON list in SATOM's application settings. The form posts every column as a parallel list; departments and networks each travel as one JSON-encoded value per row so a variable-length list cannot shift the other columns. Each segment keeps a networks list; its single cidr and gateway fields mirror the first network, so readers written for one network still read it. Rows with neither a name nor a network are dropped. Older data with a single department value is read as a one-item department list, and a segment saved before networks existed

docs.k: capacity limits headroom hard max operational cap quota model sku datasheet object limits maximum policies sizing ceiling guardrail quota users.manage
docs.s: Per model and firmware, record how many server policies, protection profiles, certificates and SNI policies a FortiWeb can hold, and set your own safety cap that clone workflows and device health check before objects are created.

docs.x: Capacity Limits is the catalog of how many objects of each kind a FortiWeb model can hold on a given firmware version. For each object type you enter Fortinet's published ceiling (the hard max ) and, optionally, your own lower operational cap . SATOM's clone workflows check this catalog before they create objects, and device health grades how close each appliance is to it.

Keeps one row per model × firmware major × object type . The object types are: Server Policies Web Protection Profiles (inline and offline profiles together) Local Certificates SNI Policies Computes the effective cap = the lower of the hard max and your operational cap. Shows In use (fleet max) : the highest count of that object type on any visible appliance of the same model and firmware major. The value is highlighted when it reaches the capacity warning level of the effective cap — the product's warning % from the monitoring thresholds settings (default 80 %). Suggests fleet models that hav

The appliance's Model and Firmware must be known in Appliances . SATOM matches a catalog by the exact model string and the firmware major ( 7.6.8 → 7.6 ). An appliance without a model or a parseable firmware has no catalog. Counts come from SATOM's local cache of the appliance's objects, so the appliance must have been synchronised at least once.

All routes (view, add, save, delete) require users.manage ( Administrator ). Without it, /capacity/ answers 403 , and the menu entry is not shown (the Administrator menu group is drawn only for users.manage ). Where it is reachable. The menu entry Capacity Limits is in the Administrator group of the FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs. The URL also opens in the Global, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs. The catalog shown is scoped to the active ADOM's product: each product ADOM shows its own product's catalogs, Global shows every product's.

Open Administrator → Capacity Limits . If the blue bar Fleet models without a limits catalog: lists your model, press its ＋ ( , ) button. Otherwise enter Model / SKU (e.g. FortiWeb-VM02, FWB-600F) , pick the Product (in a product ADOM only that product is offered; Global offers every product) and enter the Firmware major (for example 7.6 ), then press Add model . A card for the model appears with one empty row per object type. 💡 Tip Type the model exactly as it appears on the appliance in Appliances . A catalog only applies to appliances whose model string and firmware major match it. ℹ️ Note

In the model's card, for each object type: - enter Hard max (Fortinet) — the ceiling from the model's datasheet; - choose a Cap mode : no cap , number or % of max ; - enter the Cap value (an absolute number, or a percentage of the hard max). Press Save ( ) . Check Effective cap — the number automations will respect.
Press the red trash button in the model's card header. Confirm "Remove ALL limit rows for ( )?" .

Field Description Required Example Model / SKU Appliance model string Yes (add) FortiWeb-VM04 Product Product the catalog is for; only the products the active ADOM can create are offered Yes (add) FortiWeb Firmware major Major.minor firmware version Yes (add) 7.6 Hard max (Fortinet) Published ceiling; whole number ≥ 0. Blank = unknown No 2000 Cap mode no cap — only the hard max applies; number — absolute cap; % of max — percentage of the hard max No % of max Cap value For number : whole number ≥ 0, not above the hard max. For % of max : greater than 0 and at most 100 No 80 Effective cap Calcul

🧪 Example — Keep 20 % head-room on a VM04 Your FortiWeb-VM04 appliances run firmware 7.6.x. The datasheet allows 2,000 server policies. Object type Hard max Cap mode Cap value Effective cap Server Policies 2000 % of max 80 1600 A colleague later clones a policy onto fweb-01 (a VM04 on 7.6.8) that already holds 1,600 server policies. The pre-flight checklist blocks the clone with "Capacity limit reached for Server Policies on fweb-01: used 1600 + 1 would exceed cap 1600 (hard max 2000)."

Saving updates only rows that changed and stamps them with your user name; the page shows "Saved limit row(s)." or "No changes." . The Audit log records capacity.model_add , capacity.limits_update and capacity.model_delete . From then on: a clone that would exceed the effective cap is blocked with "Capacity limit reached for on : used + would exceed cap (hard max )." ; an object type with no cap set never blocks work — the check passes with "No capacity limit set for / ; allowing (used= )." ; a whole-plan clone check lists object types that have no capped type at all as unchecked , instead of

docs.h: "Model and firmware major are both required."
docs.x: Possible causes - Add model was pressed with an empty field. Solution 1. Fill in both Model / SKU and Firmware major and press Add model again. Verification - A card for the model appears with "Added ( , ) — object types ready to configure."

docs.h: "This ADOM cannot add capacity rows for ."
docs.x: Possible causes - The posted product is not one the active ADOM can create (a product ADOM can only add its own product). Solution 1. Switch to that product's ADOM, or to Global, and add the model there. Verification - The card shows the product next to the model name.
Possible causes - In number mode the cap value is above the hard max. Solution 1. Lower the cap value, or correct the hard max, and save again. Verification - Effective cap shows the cap value.

docs.h: " / : percent must be greater than 0 and at most 100" or "… must be a non-negative integer"
docs.x: Possible causes - A percentage of 0 or less, or above 100, or a hard max / number cap that is negative or not a whole number. A number of 0 is accepted. Solution 1. Correct the value. Rows with an error are skipped; the other rows of the card are saved. At most six errors are shown at once. Verification - Save again; no red message appears for the row.

docs.h: A clone is never blocked although the model is full
docs.x: Possible causes - No catalog matches the appliance: the model string or firmware major differ from the catalog's, or the appliance has no model recorded. - Only a % of max cap is set and the hard max is blank, so there is no effective cap. - The appliance's object cache is out of date. Solution 1. Compare the appliance's Model and Firmware in Appliances with the catalog card title. 2. Enter a hard max. 3. Refresh the appliance's cached configuration. Verification - The check message changes from "No capacity limit set …" to "OK: …" or a block.

docs.h: The count is higher than the objects in one ADOM
docs.x: Possible causes - The appliance is a multi-ADOM chassis. The cap belongs to the hardware, so SATOM counts the objects of all ADOM rows of the same chassis. The message then says "across ADOM rows on " . Solution 1. None needed; size the cap for the whole box. Verification - The sum of the per-ADOM counts equals the reported usage.

Advanced How counting works Counts are read from SATOM's local device-object cache, never from the live appliance. For a multi-ADOM chassis the count is summed over every row that belongs to the same chassis; if the chassis cannot be resolved, only the one row is counted. In use (fleet max) on this page is the highest such count among visible appliances of the model and firmware major. Advanced Product scope Each catalog belongs to one product, chosen with Product when the model is added (the fleet-model buttons carry the appliance's product). Each ADOM lists only its own product's catalogs; G

docs.s: The FortiADC ADOM mirrors the appliance's own left menu so you can browse, create, edit and delete FortiADC objects live on a selected device, with a dry-run preview before every form-based write.

docs.x: The FortiADC workspace is the SATOM ADOM for FortiADC application delivery controllers. Its sidebar reproduces the FortiADC GUI's own left menu (Server Load Balance, Link Load Balance, Global Load Balance, Web Application Firewall, and so on), so anyone who knows the appliance knows where to look. Every list is read live from the FortiADC you have selected: there is no local cache for FortiADC objects.

Dashboard ( /adc/ ) — a device picker with every FortiADC you may see, plus an overview card per menu section with a link to each entry. The subtitle counts the object types and sections that are available. Menu pages ( /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page> ) — one page per entry of the FortiADC's measured menu, drawn in FortiADC's layout: its tabs, its Create New menu and its columns (for example, on 7.6.7, Server Load Balance > Real Server Pool has the tabs Real Server Pool , Real Server and Server SSL ). Each tab lists the objects live from the device. Dialogs — each object opens in FortiADC's own d

The FortiADC group is the selected appliance's own menu, drawn from the GUI layout measured on its firmware build (the layouts arrive with the knowledge packs): All pages — a grid with every page of the menu, one card per top-level group. The FortiADC menu tree in the device's own order (Server Load Balance, Link Load Balance, Global Load Balance, Web Application Firewall, Network Security, Network, System and so on), one entry per page the build has. Not in GUI, but in CLI — see Not in GUI, but in CLI . Signatures — SATOM's live overview of the Web Attack Signature policies, for holders of pr

The /adc/m/<item> pages follow a fixed tree modelled on the FortiADC 8.0 GUI. Since 3.1 the sidebar no longer draws it: an old address opens the measured page that shows the same objects, where the selected appliance has one, and ?classic=1 opens the classic page. A classic entry only exists when the FortiADC endpoint registry contains at least one of its object types. Group Entries Server Load Balance Virtual Server, Real Server Pool, SSL Management, Content Management, Profiles, Advanced Profiles, Application Optimization, Scripting Link Load Balance Link Group, Link Policy, Virtual Tunnel G

Open the product selector and choose FortiADC , or click FortiADC under ADOMs in the Global sidebar. On the dashboard, find the device under FortiADC devices and click Select . The card shows the badge selected and the button changes to Selected . To change device later, click the Device entry at the top of the sidebar.

In the sidebar, open the FortiADC group, then a group of the device's menu (for example Server Load Balance ), and click a page (for example Real Server Pool ). FortiADC → All pages shows the whole menu as a grid, one card per top-level group. The breadcrumb shows the FortiADC menu path ( FortiADC / Server Load Balance / Real Server Pool ) and the header the device and its firmware. The tabs across the top are FortiADC's own (on 7.6.7: Real Server Pool , Real Server and Server SSL ). Click a tab to load it. The rows are read live from the device: the toolbar shows a live badge and the object c

Open the page and the tab for the object type. Click Create New (where FortiADC's menu offers several kinds, pick one). FortiADC's dialog opens. Fill in the name and the fields, click Save , check Review the change , then click Apply to <device> . SATOM re-reads the object and shows the verdict: Verified on the device , Not applied (naming the value the device kept) or Not verified . For a virtual server, the Wizard button on Server Load Balance → Virtual Server is usually quicker. See Guided virtual server wizard .

docs.h: Delete an object from a list
docs.x: Select the row and click Delete . Confirm Delete "<name>"? . SATOM sends a dry run and shows the request; nothing has been removed yet. Confirm Apply this delete to the device now? . SATOM deletes the object, re-reads the device, and the toast reports the verdict before the list reloads.

docs.h: Review the Web Attack Signature policies
docs.x: Open FortiADC → Signatures (the last entry of the group). The table lists each signature policy with Status , Categories , Sub-categories , Disabled sigs , High action , Medium action , Low action and Exception . Predefined policies carry a built-in badge. Click a name or the pencil button to open the policy in the object editor. Create New opens a blank Web Attack Signature policy. The device's own list of these policies is the measured page Web Application Firewall → Known Web Attacks (tab Web Attack Signature on 7.6.7).

Open the FortiADC in Appliances and click VS Inspector under Appliance Actions . Choose the source: - Live (REST) reads the device. It starts from the virtual servers and follows their references outward: each table is read once, child tables are read only for the groups a virtual server actually reaches, and the whole walk uses one reused connection. - From last rediscovery draws the same tree from the last sweep and its depth capture, without contacting the device. The header shows the sweep and the depth capture it used. Each virtual server is drawn to the end of every reference: content ro

Open Administrator → Naming . The page opens on the FortiADC product and lists the FortiADC naming elements (for example Real Server with the default pattern rs-{name} ). See Naming for how patterns work. The FortiADC patterns are reference only : the page says so in a note ( Reference only. FortiADC patterns document your convention; the FortiADC object editor and the virtual-server wizard do not fill in or check names from them. ). You type every object name yourself.

The Real Server Pool tab lists pool-web with FortiADC's columns. Double-click pool-web . FortiADC's dialog opens; its member table lists each pool member. Reads change nothing and leave no audit entry. Every write that reaches the device is recorded in the Audit Log with the FortiADC appliance and the object, for example adc.create , adc.update , adc.delete , adc.row_create , adc.row_update , adc.row_delete or adc.wizard_create . Lists are not stored: the next visit reads the device again. docs.h: "No FortiADC selected — object lists are read live from a device."
docs.x: Possible causes - No device is selected, and the ADOM holds more than one FortiADC. - No FortiADC is registered, or the one that is registered is in maintenance mode and hidden from you. Solution 1. Click Pick one on the FortiADC dashboard and select a device. 2. If the dashboard says No FortiADC appliances registered yet , register the appliance with kind fortiadc under Administrator → Appliances (or Operations → Appliances without the administrator capability). Verification — the FortiADC group of the sidebar shows the device's menu, and its pages show a live badge.

docs.h: "Device error: HTTP 401" or "Device error: device errcode …"
docs.x: Possible causes - Wrong credentials on the appliance record (HTTP 401). - The device refused the read and returned a negative error code. - The object type does not exist on this FortiADC build (HTTP 404). Solution 1. Check the appliance credentials under Administrator → Appliances (or Operations → Appliances ). 2. If one tab fails and the others work, check the endpoint in the FortiADC API catalog and disable or correct it (see Product API pages ). Verification — after ⟳ the tab lists objects instead of the error (on a measured page, <device> did not answer: … ; on a classic page, the red ban

Possible causes — the registry records that the object type is not available on the firmware build the device runs. Solution — check the API versions page of the FortiADC API catalog, or pick a device on a build that serves the type. Verification — the tab lists objects instead of the error banner.

docs.h: A menu entry or tab is missing
docs.x: Possible causes - No GUI layout for the device's build has been imported: the FortiADC group then holds Signatures only. - The device's build has no such page in its own GUI, or the layout was refused on import. - An administrator hid monitor or device-managed pages under Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus . Solution 1. Check that the knowledge packs are up to date. 2. Check ADOM Menus . 3. A bookmark to the classic page ( /adc/m/<item>?classic=1 ) still opens it. Verification — the page appears in the FortiADC group and in All pages .

Possible causes — the Signatures page requires protection.view , and your profile does not have it. Solution — ask an administrator to add protection.view to your profile. The built-in Viewer, Operator and Administrator profiles have it. Verification — the page lists the signature policies.

Advanced How lists and columns are built The menu is the FortiADC GUI layout measured on the device's firmware build, delivered by the knowledge packs; it is cached for 60 seconds per product and build. The page's tabs, Create New menu and columns are the layout's. Each tab is one live read of its collection on the device; nothing is cached, and ⟳ only drops the few-second read memo. On the classic /adc/m/<item> pages ( ?classic=1 ), the menu tree lives in code and is resolved against the FortiADC registry ( product = fortiadc ), and columns are derived from the first object in the response: t

docs.s: Edit any FortiADC object live in a form, manage its child tables such as pool members, and preview the exact REST request before it is applied.

docs.x: The object editor opens one FortiADC object read live from the selected device. It shows the object's fields as a form, lists the child tables the object owns (for example a pool's members) and keeps a raw JSON editor for anything the form cannot edit. Form-based saves are dry-run first : you see the exact REST call before anything is sent. ℹ️ Note Changed in 3.1.0: the sidebar's FortiADC group draws the FortiADC's own measured menu, whose pages open each object in FortiADC's own dialog (see FortiADC workspace ). This editor opens from FortiADC → Signatures and from the classic menu pages, whi

Settings card — every scalar field of the object, with widgets inferred from the device's values: enable / disable becomes a toggle, numbers become number boxes, everything else is text. The identity ( mkey ) is shown in the page title and is not editable. Structured values (read-only — edit via Raw JSON) — fields whose value is a list or an object. They are displayed but cannot be changed in the form. Child-table cards — one card per child table of the object type (for example Pool Members , Group Members , Match Conditions , Rules ). Each row can be saved or deleted, and new rows can be adde

A FortiADC selected in the ADOM. Without one the editor redirects to the FortiADC dashboard. The object type must exist in the FortiADC endpoint registry. Unknown types return 404. A type added, re-enabled or disabled on the FortiADC API page is picked up by the editor within 60 seconds, without a restart.

If you changed nothing, the editor says No changes to save.

Advanced How child tables are found FortiADC exposes a child table as its own endpoint named <parent>_child_<table> , addressed with ?pkey=<parent name> . SATOM treats every registry endpoint with that shape as a child table of <parent> — as long as <parent> is itself a registered endpoint. No separate list is kept. Advanced What the form never writes Keys starting with _ (device-internal flags such as _nondeletable ) are never shown or written. List and object values are not sent by form saves; FortiADC keeps absent keys as they are, so those values stay untouched.

docs.x: Possible causes — one of the names (virtual server, pool or a real server) already exists on the device. Solution — change the listed names, or create only the missing pieces in the object editor . Verification — Preview plan shows the plan.

docs.h: "Cannot proceed" with a list of errors
docs.x: Possible causes — validation failed. The messages are, for example, Virtual server name is required. , Pool name is required. , Virtual server IP address is required. , Virtual server IP "…" is not a valid IP. , Real server #2: IP address is required. , At least one real server (back-end) is required. or Real server names must be unique within the batch. Solution — correct the fields named in the messages. Verification — the card title changes to Plan — N REST call(s) .

Possible causes — the device refused one call (for example an unknown profile or interface). The card shows the failed step, the device error and Rolled back: … with the objects that were removed again. Solution 1. Read the device error and fix the value (profile, method, interface…). 2. Check the list on the device: rollback is best effort, so an object whose delete also failed is not listed under Rolled back . 3. Run the wizard again. Verification — Create all ends with the Created card.

Advanced Order and rollback The plan is built without any device access. On Create all the wizard first lists each object type once to detect name conflicts (HTTP 409 when it finds one), then creates each step in order. On the first failure it deletes what it created in reverse order (pool members with ?pkey= ), ignoring delete errors, and returns HTTP 502 with failed_step , created and rolled_back .

The unit answers with a task id, and SATOM polls /task/task/<id> every 1.5 seconds for up to 45 seconds. The task counts as failed when its state is 5 or 7, when num_err is above zero, or when a line carries an error. docs.x: The FortiGate workspace is the SATOM ADOM for FortiGate firewalls. It shows a FortiGate's configuration live, in the layout of the device's own GUI, and reads everything from the FortiGate you selected: SATOM keeps no FortiGate configuration cache. SATOM 3.0 shipped it read-only; the measured GUI pages now edit cmdb objects (dry run first, read back and verified), and an API console sends cmdb writes, dry-run by default. The section pages stay read-only.

Dashboard ( /fgt/ ): the FortiGate devices you can see, with Select , the live Unit status of the selected unit (hostname, firmware, build, serial, model, log disk) and a map of every section. These pages write : Create New , edit, Clone and Delete of a cmdb object, and the rows of its inline tables, as POST / PUT / DELETE on /api/v2/cmdb/<path> . Every save is a dry run first; the apply is audited and read back. Mon

A FortiGate reachable over HTTPS from SATOM. A REST API administrator on the FortiGate and its token ( execute api-user generate-key <api-user> ). FortiOS 8.0 refuses password logins on the REST API. A read-only admin profile is enough to read everything. The token's profile also decides what a write may do: give it a read-write profile only if operators are to edit from SATOM. A licensed FortiGate-VM: an unlicensed VM answers 401 to every REST call except its licence status. SATOM's address in the API user's trusted hosts, if you restrict them.

docs.x: SATOM's monitoring area is a set of pages that each answer one question about your appliances or about SATOM itself: is the box alive , is the service serving , how much is it carrying , what changed , which layer is broken . Almost every page reads data SATOM has already stored, so opening a page never contacts an appliance; the measuring is done by background jobs and scheduled actions. This page is a map. Each feature has its own article.

Every monitoring page filters its rows through the set of appliances the current ADOM may see. In the FortiWeb ADOM you see FortiWeb devices and the probes, targets and reports that belong to them; in the Global ADOM you see every product. A probe created from the Global ADOM against a FortiADC appears in the FortiADC ADOM automatically. Two pages are deliberately Global-only : SATOM health (it names node hostnames and infrastructure addresses) and Sentinel . Opening /monitoring/satom from a product ADOM redirects you to Device health.

Monitoring → Fleet health → Device health (URL /monitoring/ ) shows one card per appliance with a status badge — healthy , warning , critical or unknown — and the reasons behind it. The badge is the worst of four signals: Signal (label on the card) What it measures Harvest the last scheduled configuration syncs of the device Cache the age of the newest stored configuration snapshot Deep monitors the worst status of the device's enabled probes Capacity object counts against the admin cap A device about which nothing has been measured shows unknown , never healthy. Above the cards, warning and c

Monitoring → Fleet health → SATOM health (URL /monitoring/satom , Global ADOM only) describes the installation, not the appliances: Infrastructure health — HA nodes, the Git repository and the external backup server, probed after the page has loaded. Resource history — CPU, memory and disk of every node over 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 days, 30 days or 90 days, one chart per resource with all nodes on it and the warning and critical limits as dashed lines (see below). Database — engine, version, size, latency, table row counts, the age of the nightly dump (amber when older than 30 hours) and the number

The node tiles show each node's CPU, memory and disk now ; Resource history keeps those same readings over time , for the primary and the standby. The metrics_scrape scheduled action (every 3 minutes) samples both nodes into the local metrics store and mirrors the samples to the peer node, so a promoted standby keeps the history. If that action is paused, the charts stop growing. Its run summary says how many node samples it wrote, or why it could not write them. A node that did not answer leaves a gap in the line. Its last reading is never carried forward. Each point also looks six minutes fu

A fresh install seeds no scheduled actions until the node gets its first appliance; SATOM then creates the standard plan, if the node has no System Automation yet. When a schedule is missing the pages say so (for example the Reports page shows not scheduled ). The command sudo satom execute seed actions --yes fills the gaps; see Scheduled actions . docs.x: Metrics is a statistics page for the active ADOM. It answers two questions over a date range: how much activity was there (audited actions, configuration changes, users, appliances touched) and how many objects exist (server policies, backends, protection profiles, certificates — labelled per product). It reads the audit log, the change history and stored inventory snapshots, so it never contacts an appliance (one exception: FortiADC counts, see Advanced ). ℹ️ Note Despite the name, this page is not the time-series metrics store. Device telemetry (CPU, sessions, throughput…) is collected on Me

Four summary cards : Total Actions , Config Changes , Active Users , Appliances Touched for the period. Four inventory cards showing total now , labelled per ADOM. Inventory Totals per Day — how many objects existed each day (daily snapshots). Activity Timeline — audit actions and configuration changes per day. docs.s: The shared engine behind Deep monitors and Service Monitor — creating, discovering, running, muting and charting probes, how statuses and thresholds are decided, and how long history is kept.

docs.x: A probe is one check against one thing — a URL, a device's CPU, a server policy's sessions, a FortiAuthenticator licence pool — that runs on a schedule, grades the result ( ok , warn , crit , error , unknown ) and stores every result as a time series. Two pages show probes: Deep monitors (checks that reach into the box: synthetic HTTPS, interfaces, CPU, memory, proxyd ) and Service Monitor (telemetry read over the appliance's REST monitor API). They are two views of one subsystem: same storage, same runner, same deep_monitor scheduled action. This article covers what they share.

Runs each enabled probe when its interval has elapsed, as part of the deep_monitor sweep. Stores a sample per run (status, value, detail, raw payload) and keeps hourly and daily roll-ups for long charts. Feeds the Deep monitors signal of Device health , the device findings of Alerting , Analytics rule panels and Monitoring reports . Lets you create probes by hand or discover them from a device, mute one temporarily, and open a chart of any probe.

At least one registered appliance (a bare URL probe on Deep monitors needs none). The deep_monitor scheduled action ( Deep monitors — probe sweep ) for automatic runs. It is in the standard seed plan at every 3 minutes ; a fresh install has none until you seed or create it — see Scheduled actions .

🔑 Permission Viewing probes, charts and history: the legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view ; all system profiles have it. A custom profile with no read key gets 403 . Discover from device , Add probe , Probe now , edit, enable/disable, unmute and delete: the legacy config_write gate (for example operations.apply or appliances.apply ; full list in Monitoring overview ). Without it these buttons are not rendered and the endpoints return 403 . Each page only accepts its own kinds: a probe id that belongs to the other page answers 404 ( no such probe on this page ). ℹ

Click Discover from device . Pick the device and tick the sets you want (they differ per page — see Deep monitors and Service Monitor ). Click Discover . A job runs in the background; the result ( N service probe(s) (M already present) …) arrives in the notification bell and the table reloads. Discovery is idempotent: probes that already exist are left alone.

docs.h: Add or edit a probe by hand
docs.x: Click Add probe (or the pencil icon on a row). Choose the Type , give it a Name , pick the Device , and fill the fields for that type. Set Interval (min) (default 3 , the seeded sweep interval) and Timeout (s) . Optionally mute it (see below). Click Save .

Probe now in the header runs every enabled probe of this page for the devices visible in this ADOM. The play icon on a row runs that one probe. Both run as a background job. A successful run is silent (the table reloads); a failed sweep sends <page> sweep failed: … to the bell.

In the edit form, set Mute this probe (hours) (maximum 720) and a reason ( why (recorded and shown on the row) ), then Save . The row shows a muted chip. To lift it early, click the bell icon ( Unmute ) on the row; it appears only on muted probes and is recorded in the audit log. Editing the probe and setting the hours to 0 or empty also works. A muted probe keeps running and keeps its own status; it stops raising the device badge and the alert mail. There is no permanent mute.

Click a sparkline to open the chart: 1 h , 24 h , 7 days , 30 days , or From date / To date and Apply . The chart draws threshold lines and states which source it used (raw, hourly, daily). Click the Last result text to open History : the last 200 samples and the Latest raw payload .
Use the pause/play and trash icons on the row. A disabled probe is greyed and not run by the sweep.

🧪 Example — Watch CPU on a new FortiWeb with the product defaults Discover from device → fweb-02 → keep Device baseline ticked → Discover . The bell reports baseline: interface, cpu, memory, proxyd . The CPU probe's warn/crit boxes are empty, so it inherits the FortiWeb values from Settings → Thresholds. Raise the FortiWeb CPU limit there and this probe follows immediately.

Creating, editing, toggling, unmuting and deleting a probe writes an audit entry ( deep_monitor.create , service_monitor.update , …). Each run stores one sample and updates the probe's last status. The worst enabled, non-muted probe of a device becomes the Deep monitors signal on Device health and is mailed by the alert engine.

docs.s: Checks that reach into the appliance — a synthetic HTTPS request to a published service, interface IP/link drift, processor load, memory usage and the proxyd daemon — each stored as a time series with its own thresholds.

docs.x: Deep monitors answers is the service actually serving? Each probe either sends a synthetic request through the published front end, reads the device's interfaces from SATOM's cache, or runs a read-only CLI command on the appliance. Results are stored as time series because the interesting signal is usually a value changing — an IP that moved, a daemon that restarted. All probe mechanics (discover, add, mute, charts, statuses, retention) are shared with Service Monitor and described in Probes .

Advanced Notes The HTTPS kind requests any URL you enter; it is not limited to inventory hosts. The interface target field holds at most 120 characters of port names; a list that does not fit drops whole names at the end rather than truncating a name. The REST-telemetry kinds (sessions, throughput, transactions, licence, tokens) live on Service Monitor . The two pages share one sweep, so do not schedule a second one.

docs.s: Runtime telemetry read over the appliance's REST monitor API — box sessions, per-policy sessions, latency and backend health, throughput and HTTP transactions on FortiWeb; licence headroom and FortiToken pools on FortiAuthenticator — graded against thresholds.

docs.x: Service Monitor answers how much is each service carrying right now? Every probe here is a REST call to the appliance's monitor API — no SSH and no configuration API — so it keeps reporting on a FortiWeb whose configuration API is refusing calls (for example an expired licence). docs.x: A monitoring report is a stored summary of one complete period — a day, an ISO week (Monday to Sunday) or a calendar month, in UTC — built from the probe samples and roll-ups and from the local metrics store. Reports are stored , not recomputed when you open them: raw samples expire, and a summary rebuilt months later would silently use coarser data. ℹ️ Note This page is about monitoring summaries. For SQL-style reports over the SATOM database see Database tools ; for user-submitted problem reports see Bug reports .

docs.s: The proactive alert engine evaluates health checks every 15 minutes and routes each finding to five sinks — in-app bell, e-mail, a signed webhook, integration hooks and a syslog/CEF feed — each with its own severity floor and family mask.

docs.x: Every other monitoring page is pull : you open it and read it. The alert engine is push : a systemd timer ( satom-alerts.timer ) runs it every 15 minutes on every node ; it evaluates a set of health checks and sends each new finding to the people and systems that asked for it, so nobody has to be looking at a page.

Check (label) Raises a finding when… Family Cert expiry this node's TLS certificate has ≤ Cert warn (days) left, or a renewal failed cert Git divergence the standby lags more than Git behind max commits, or a local commit stays unpushed longer than Git unpushed max (hours) git Device health a device is degraded or critical on the same ladder as Device health , plus a live TCP probe of its port (devices in maintenance are skipped). One finding per device, listing every failing signal — not one per signal. When a deep monitor is behind it, the title carries the reading and the limit crossed ( De

Sink Default Notes In-app bell on, info , all families to every admin-capable user; ignores the master switch Email on, info , all families needs Enable alert dispatch ; one mail per run Webhook (HTTP POST) off needs the master switch; one POST per run with every accepted finding Integration hooks off needs the master switch; one alert.fired event per finding — enqueued, not delivered Syslog / CEF feed off no cooldown, runs on the standby too, ignores the master switch Each sink has exactly two filters: a Minimum severity ( info , warning , critical ) and Families delivered . A sink with no fa

A finding that reached at least one notification sink is suppressed for Cooldown (hours) (default 6). The syslog feed has no cooldown. Device and host findings include the status in their key, so an escalation from warning to critical is delivered even inside the cooldown.

docs.s: Resolve a list of host names or IPs against your configured DNS servers and, in the same step, find which FortiWeb server policy or FortiADC virtual server publishes them — with links to the policy, DNS record management and a guarded service decommission.

docs.x: DNS & LB Lookup takes up to 50 host names or IP addresses and answers two questions at once: What does DNS say? — each entry is resolved with dig against every DNS server configured for this site. Who publishes it? — each entry is matched against the load-balancing configuration of the fleet: FortiWeb server policies (from SATOM's cache) and FortiADC virtual servers (read live). From a match you can open the policy, manage DNS records in an external DNS backend, or decommission the whole service.

Resolves each entry against each enabled DNS server (A by default; reverse lookup for IPs; name TYPE for another type such as CNAME ). A wildcard *.example.com is probed as example.example.com . Shows LB matches : product, gateway, ADOM, policy/virtual server, service IP, HTTP/HTTPS service, pool, members, certificate CN, SNI, WAF policy, App ID, comment, status, zone, line, department — plus a mini path policy → pool → backends coloured by configured status. Quick LB shows only the gateway(s). Copy DNS / Copy LB copy tab-separated results for a spreadsheet. Lists entries Not found in any sour

At least one DNS server configured in Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup (none are shipped). Until then the page says No DNS servers configured. For FortiWeb matches: harvested configuration (the page reads the cache). For DNS Records : a DNS backend in Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Records .

🔑 Permission Lookup (opening the page): network.view ; all system profiles have it. Without it the sidebar link is hidden and the page answers 403 . Results are limited to the appliances of the current ADOM (Global sees all). Manage in Settings → DNS Lookup (the server list) and DNS Records : users.manage ( Administrator ). The button and link are hidden otherwise; the endpoints return 403 . Decommission : the legacy config_write gate (e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply ); the button only appears for FortiWeb and FortiADC matches. ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: DNS & LB Lookup now requires

Open Operations → DNS Lookup . Paste entries into Hostnames / IPs — one per line (optionally name TYPE ). Choose Options : Show LB matches (default on), Quick LB (gateway only) , Exact match , Show TTL . Click Search . Reset clears the form. Expand a match to see the details; Open policy opens the FortiWeb policy in a new tab.

Click DNS Records in the Results header. Choose the Backend (if several are configured), enter Name (FQDN) , Zone , View as offered by the backend, and click Load . Edit a record or fill Type , Value , TTL and click Save record ; New clears the form. Delete from the list.

On a match, click Decommission . SATOM builds a plan : every object that would be deleted, kept or unbound, with warnings. Read the plan. If it carries warnings, tick I have read the warnings above and accept the shared dependencies they name. Type the policy name in type the policy name to confirm . Click Delete everything listed . Results are shown per object.

Field Description Required Example Hostnames / IPs One per line; characters outside letters, digits, space and . : * _ - / are removed; max 50 entries Yes www.example.com Show LB matches Match each entry against LB configuration No on Quick LB (gateway only) Show only the gateway column No off Exact match Whole-value (or comma-separated token) match instead of substring No off Show TTL Append (TTL:n) to DNS answers No off DNS servers (Settings → DNS Lookup): a list of name + server address with an enabled flag.

🧪 Example — Who serves api.example.com, and retire it Enter api.example.com , keep Show LB matches , click Search . Both DNS servers return 192.0.2.40 ; one match shows FortiWeb fweb-01 , policy pol-api , pool pool-api with two backends. Click Decommission : the plan lists the A record, the policy, its pool, the certificate ( keep — also used by another policy), and the WAF profile. Type pol-api and click Delete everything listed .

Lookups change nothing and are not audited. DNS record changes write audit entries dns_records.create , .update , .delete . Every decommission attempt writes dns_decommission.apply (successful or refused). Objects are deleted in this order: DNS records, server policy / virtual server, SNI, certificate, WAF policy, carve-outs. If the policy itself fails to delete, nothing after it is attempted.

Advanced Data sources and matching FortiWeb LB rows come from the device cache (no device call); FortiADC rows are read live, read-only. Matching compares the entry and its wildcard-resolved form against every column of every LB row (substring by default). The App ID column is taken from the policy/virtual-server comment ( AppID: <token> , app-id=… , or a bracketed [APP-123] ). dig runs with a 2-second timeout and one try per server; lookups run in parallel (up to 8).

docs.s: Paste or upload a list of source;policy;destination lines and SATOM checks, per line, whether the real servers behind each FortiWeb server policy answer — on the source box and then on the destination box — without writing anything.

docs.x: Backend Reachability answers one question per line of a list: do the real servers behind this FortiWeb server policy answer — on the source appliance, and then on the destination appliance? It reads the pool members of each policy from each box and probes them. It needs no workspace tab or selected appliance, and it writes nothing : no clone, no migration, no configuration change. Typical use: before or after migrating policies from one FortiWeb to another.

Reads each line source;policy;destination (up to 200 lines). On the source first, then the destination : reads the policy's pool members and probes each one. Probes from two vantages , never merged: this node — a TCP connection from SATOM to the member's port (always on; a refused port proves the host is up); the appliance — execute ping over SSH from each box (optional). Gives each line one verdict — error , down , mismatch , unknown , ok — plus every finding that earned it. If the destination does not have the policy and SSH is on, the source's backends are pinged from the destination instea
FortiWeb appliances registered in the current ADOM, reachable over their API. For the appliance vantage: SSH credentials on the appliances.

🔑 Permission Requires the legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example monitoring.view ); all system profiles have it. Appliance names are resolved only among the appliances visible in the current ADOM. Each run is written to the audit log because it sends real traffic to third-party hosts.

Open Operations → Troubleshooting → Backend Reachability (Global ADOM or FortiWeb ADOM; until 2026-10-14 it sat under Operations → Troubleshooting in the FortiWeb ADOM). Under Lines to check , type or paste lines in One service per line , or use …or upload the file ( .txt , .csv , .tsv , max 256 KB). An uploaded file replaces the box, and the box is refilled with it. Under Vantages , optionally tick Ask each appliance too ( execute ping over SSH) . Set TCP timeout (s) and Time budget (s) if needed. Click Check . Reset clears the page.

Field Description Required Example Lines source;policy;destination ; # lines ignored; a two-field line ( source;policy ) checks the source only; a format header line is skipped Yes fweb-01;pol-shop;fweb-02 Ask each appliance too Adds the SSH execute ping vantage No off TCP timeout (s) Per-connection timeout, 0.5–10 No 2 Time budget (s) Total run budget, 10–300 No 120 Appliance names are matched case-insensitively against appliance names first, then hosts . Only FortiWeb appliances are accepted.

Verdict Typical findings error malformed line, source/destination not found or unreadable, policy absent on the source, pool unreadable down a member is unreachable mismatch policy absent on the destination, member missing or extra on the destination, no pool, empty pool, all members disabled unknown no vantage could probe, comparison skipped ok every backend answered (a source-only line is complete when the source answers)

🧪 Example — Pre-migration check of three services # source;policy;destination fweb-01;pol-shop;fweb-02 fweb-01;pol-api;fweb-02 fweb-02;pol-origin With SSH on, line 1 is ok , line 2 is mismatch (destination lacks member 198.51.100.12:8443 ), line 3 is a source-only check.

The page shows the Report with line count, elapsed time, vantages, and per-verdict totals. An audit entry reachability.batch records the number of lines, totals, whether SSH was used, elapsed time and whether the budget was hit.
