docs.s: Search Fortinet's known and resolved issues for FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate firmware, compare two versions before an upgrade, and read the release-note prose — from a corpus SATOM imports from signed packs.

docs.x: Release Notes is a window for Fortinet's own release notes of the appliance firmware — FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer or FortiGate, matching the ADOM you are in. It lists known and resolved issues across versions, tells you what a move from one version to another resolves and what stays known, and lets you search the release-note text. Since SATOM 3.0 the corpus comes only from signed packs : the API pack that ships with each release, and the rolling knowledge pack fetched from the knowledge feed or uploaded by hand ( Knowledge packs ). SATOM itself no longer contacts an

Three tabs: Tab What it answers Issues Every known and resolved issue, filterable by version, status ( Known / Resolved ), topic and free text (bug id, description, workaround) Upgrade advisor Pick Current: and → Target: , click Show advisory : the issues the move resolves, the issues still known in the target, and the relevant upgrade notes Notes The prose sections of a release (for example what's new and upgrade notes), by version and section, with search The Upgrade advisor tab can also show Upgrade Advisory verdicts above the bug diff — rule-based checks of the upgrade notes that flag what

You are in the FortiWeb , FortiADC , FortiAuthenticator , FortiAnalyzer or FortiGate ADOM. The menu entry is not offered in Global. An imported pack. A fresh installation imports the release's API pack; the knowledge pack arrives from the feed (online) or by upload (air-gapped).

Action Needs Open the window, use the three tabs, Reload corpus Read access — any view permission, for example monitoring.view Knowledge packs… (and everything on that card) users.manage Switch Path Diagnostics (includes the Upgrade Advisory) on or off users.manage (the switch is disabled for others)

In the product's ADOM, open Tools → Release Notes . On Issues , pick a version and/or status, or type in Search bug id / description / workaround … . Read Version , Status , Bug ID , Topic and Description . The version pickers also list the builds your appliances of this product run, marked as having no notes here, when the corpus lacks them.

Open Upgrade advisor . Choose Current: and → Target: versions (they must differ). Click Show advisory . Read the Upgrade Advisory verdicts (if Path Diagnostics is on), then the resolved issues, the issues still known in the target, and the notes.

Click Knowledge packs… . On the Knowledge packs card, click Check now , then Import . Back in the window, click Reload corpus . On an air-gapped network, upload the knowledge pack instead ( Knowledge packs ).

🧪 Example — Before a FortiWeb maintenance window You run 7.6.2 and plan 7.6.4. In Upgrade advisor , Current 7.6.2 , Target 7.6.4 , Show advisory : the list shows the issues fixed between the two and the issues still open in 7.6.4, followed by the upgrade notes for that release. The line above the tabs reads Knowledge from satom-apipack-kb-20261008 (2026-10-08) , so the advice is current.

Nothing is written by reading. Reload corpus is recorded in the audit log as release_notes.reload ; the Path Diagnostics switch as scout.switch . A pack import merges its release notes into the corpus on this node. In a high-availability pair, import on the primary; the standby receives the corpus through data replication.

docs.h: "No release notes for this build in the local corpus — import a newer knowledge pack (Software Update → Knowledge packs)."
docs.x: Possible causes - No imported pack carries notes for that build yet (a very new build, or a node whose knowledge pack is old). Solution 1. An administrator imports the newest knowledge pack ( Knowledge packs ). 2. Click Reload corpus . Verification - The window lists the build's issues.

docs.h: "No corpus on this node yet — import a knowledge pack (Software Update → Knowledge packs). It is not fetched from git."
docs.x: Possible causes - No pack with release notes was imported on this node (for example the installer's pack import was skipped). Solution 1. Import the release's own pack ( sudo satom execute apipack import shipped --yes ) or a knowledge pack.

Possible causes - The newest knowledge pack on this node is older than 30 days: the daily fetch is off, failing, or the node is air-gapped. Solution 1. Check Software Update → Knowledge packs → Last check . 2. Import a newer pack.

docs.h: The advisory says sections "were not read"
docs.x: Possible causes - The corpus lacks a section the advisory needs for a version in the range. Solution 1. Import a newer knowledge pack and ask again. The advisory is never called clean while coverage is missing.

docs.h: "Pick a current and a target version." / "Pick two different versions."
docs.x: Possible causes - One version is missing, or both are the same.

docs.h: "Turn on Path Diagnostics in Settings → Path Diagnostics to see the Upgrade Advisory."
docs.x: Possible causes - Path Diagnostics is switched off for the site, and the Upgrade Advisory follows that switch. Solution 1. A user with users.manage ticks Path Diagnostics (includes the Upgrade Advisory) in this window, or switches on Path Diagnostics is available in Settings → Path Diagnostics → Settings ( Path Diagnostics settings ). Verification - The window shows the toast Path Diagnostics on: the Upgrade Advisory is available. and Show advisory returns verdicts again.

Removed in SATOM 3.0, together with version discovery and its routes. Crawling the vendor documentation is done only by the SATOM team's separate Knowledge Harvester ; its result reaches you as packs. If you kept outbound access to the vendor documentation site only for SATOM, it is no longer needed.

Advanced Scope, storage and corrections Every product's rows are stored in one corpus file, tagged per product; every read is filtered to the ADOM you are in. A pack import adds the versions the node does not hold, and replaces a version an earlier pack wrote when a pack built from a newer snapshot carries a different copy — that is how corrections arrive. A version this node scanned itself before 3.0 is local data and is never replaced. Which pack wrote each version is recorded with the corpus. The corpus is local to each node and is not stored in git.

docs.k: users accounts profiles roles rbac permissions anti-lockout readonly operator admin disable user clone profile user management roles access rights permission sets groups rights privileges add user rbac users.manage profiles.manage users.view
docs.s: Create and manage SATOM accounts and compose the permission profiles that decide exactly what each account may do, with a guard that never lets you remove the last administrator.

docs.x: Every person who signs in to SATOM has a user account , and every account is assigned exactly one permission profile . The profile is a named set of granular permissions (for example View protection , Apply network , Manage users ) and it is the only thing that decides what the user can see and do. Three system profiles ship with SATOM — readonly , operator and admin — and administrators can compose any number of custom profiles on top of them.

Users lists every account with its profile, creation date, last login and status, and lets an administrator add, enable/disable, re-profile and delete accounts, reset a local account's password, clear its two-factor authentication and unlock it after failed sign-ins. Holders of users.view alone see the same list read-only. Profiles lists every profile with its type ( System / Custom ), the Effective role it behaves like, how many permissions it grants and how many users carry it. Custom profiles can be created, edited, cloned and deleted; system profiles can be viewed and cloned. An anti-locko

To manage users you need users.manage ; to manage profiles you need profiles.manage . A fresh install seeds one administrator account, admin , on the admin profile (see First login ). Directory accounts (Active Directory / LDAP / RADIUS) are not created here: they are created automatically at first sign-in or imported under Settings → Authentication . Once they exist they appear in the Users list and are managed exactly like local accounts.

🔑 Permission Users ( /users/ and Settings → Access & Identity → Users ): the list opens with users.view or users.manage ; every action (add, enable/disable, change profile, reset password, clear 2FA, unlock, delete) requires users.manage . With users.view only, the page shows Read-only view instead of Add User , the Actions column is hidden, and the sidebar shows a Users entry above Settings . With neither key, /users/ returns 403 Forbidden . The Access & Identity group of Settings is shown only to users.manage holders. Profiles ( /profiles/ and Settings → Access & Identity → Profiles ): every

Profile Shown as What it grants readonly Read Only "Read-only access to every section. Cannot change anything." The view keys of every area: monitoring.view , protection.view , network.view , operations.view , backups.view , registry.view , audit.view , appliances.view . operator Operator "Read everything plus manage appliances, protection, network, backups and operations. No user or registry administration." Everything in readonly plus advisor.use , backups.create , backups.restore , protection.edit , protection.apply , network.edit , network.apply , operations.apply , operations.template_sav

The profile editor groups the catalog into twelve areas, in this order: Monitoring, Web Protection, Network, Operations, Backups, API Registry, Audit Log, Appliances, Studio, Users, Profiles, Scout (AI assistant). Keys marked with a shield icon (tooltip Administrative capability ) are the sensitive ones: operations.template_approve , appliances.view_maintenance , studio.python_console , studio.plugin_studio , studio.lua_studio , users.manage , profiles.manage and advisor.configure . The icon is informational; it does not restrict who can tick the box.

Open Settings and expand Access & Identity , then choose Users or Profiles . The same panels are also available as stand-alone pages at /users/ (sidebar → Administrator → Users , in the Global and FortiADC workspaces) and /profiles/ .

docs.h: Share apps and Wiki articles with a group
docs.x: Administrator → Access → Groups keeps named sets of users ( users.manage ). Python Studio apps are shared with groups or with people, and a Wiki article can be limited to groups: add a colleague to a group and they get every app and article of that group. New group → name, description, members → Save . A group an app is shared with cannot be deleted until it is removed from the app (the message names the apps). The Wiki articles column counts the articles naming each group; deleting such a group is allowed and leaves those articles closed (author and Wiki moderators only), never open to everyo

docs.h: Confine a profile to some ADOMs
docs.x: Open the profile ( Profiles → the profile's name). System profiles cannot be edited: clone one first. In the ADOMs card tick the ADOMs this profile may work in. With none ticked it may work in every ADOM, which is what every profile had before. Click Save permissions . The ADOMs column of the profile list shows the result ( All , or one badge per ADOM). What a confined profile gets: The ADOM switcher and the sidebar list only its ADOMs. Opening any other ADOM — by link, URL or X-ADOM header — is refused with Your profile does not include the … ADOM (403 for API callers). Its Global console is

On Users , click Add User . Enter Username , Password (at least 12 characters) and Confirm Password . Pick a Profile . readonly is preselected; system profiles are suffixed " — system". Click Create User . The flash reads "User <name> created."

In the user's row click the badge icon (tooltip Change Profile ). In the Change Profile dialog pick the new profile and click Save Profile . The flash reads "<name> is now on profile “<profile>”." The new permissions apply from the user's next request.

Click the pause icon ( Disable ) or play icon ( Enable ) in the user's row. A disabled account cannot sign in; the login page tells it "This account is disabled." Enabling a directory account that is pending approval is how you approve it.

Shown only for local accounts; directory accounts change their password in the directory. In the user's row click the key icon (tooltip Reset password ). In the Reset password dialog enter the new password (at least 12 characters) twice and click Set password . The flash reads "Password for <name> reset successfully." The user signs in with the new password; the change is audited as user.reset_password .

Use this when a user has lost their authenticator. The phone icon (tooltip Clear 2FA ) appears only for accounts with two-factor authentication enabled. Click Clear 2FA and confirm "Clear two-factor authentication for '<name>'? They will sign in with their password only until they enrol again." The flash reads "Two-factor authentication cleared for <name>." The secret and the backup codes are removed (audited as user.clear_2fa ). The user can enrol again under Settings → My account .

After failed sign-ins the Status column shows a warning badge: N failed while the counter is running, Locked once the account is locked out. In the user's row click the open-lock icon (tooltip Unlock ) and confirm "Clear the sign-in lockout of '<name>'?" The flash reads "Sign-in lockout cleared for <name>." The failed-attempt counter and the lock are cleared (audited as user.unlock , with the previous values). Unlock changes nothing else: a disabled or pending-approval account stays disabled until you click Enable .

Click the trash icon ( Delete ) and confirm "Permanently delete user '<name>'? This cannot be undone." On your own row, Disable , Change Profile and Delete are replaced by Current user : you cannot disable, re-profile or delete yourself from this table. Unlock , Reset password and Clear 2FA still appear there when they apply.

Type in Search users… to filter by any visible text, or choose a role in the All Roles filter ( Admin , Operator , Read Only ). Filtering happens in the browser. Directory accounts carry a badge with their source (for example LDAP ); your own account carries You .

On Profiles , click New Profile . Enter a Profile name (required, unique, case-insensitive) and an optional Description , then click Create & set permissions . On the profile page, tick the permissions the profile should grant. Use Select all / Clear all to start from either end. Click Save permissions . The flash reads "Profile “<name>” updated."
Click the Clone icon on any profile, system or custom. SATOM creates "<name> copy" (or "<name> copy 2", "copy 3" … if that name is taken) with the same permissions and opens it for editing.

Click the eye icon (system profile, View permissions ) or the pencil icon (custom profile, Edit permissions ). System profiles open read-only with the note "System profiles are managed automatically and shown read-only."
Click the trash icon and confirm "Delete profile '<name>'? This cannot be undone." The button is disabled while users are still assigned to the profile; reassign them first.

Field Description Required Example Username Sign-in name. Must not already exist. Yes jsmith Password Local password, 12 to 1024 characters (length only, no character-class rule); stored as a scrypt hash. A shorter password is refused. Yes — Confirm Password Must match Password when filled. Yes (in the form) — Profile The permission profile. Defaults to readonly . No operator

Field Description Required Example Profile name / Name Unique name (case-insensitive), up to 64 characters. Yes WAF Editor Description Free text shown under the name in the Profiles table. No Edits WAF profiles, cannot push Permissions One checkbox per key in the catalog, grouped by area. A new profile starts with none. No View protection + Edit protection

Column Meaning Profile Name, description and an admin-capable badge when the profile holds both users.manage and profiles.manage . Type System or Custom . Effective role Admin if the profile grants users.manage ; otherwise Operator if it grants any key that implies the config_write gate (edit/apply protection or network, run operations, the template keys, edit/run appliances); otherwise Read Only — even if it grants, for example, backups.create or registry.edit . Permissions Number of keys granted. Users Number of accounts on the profile.

🧪 Example — A WAF editor who can stage but not push Profiles → New Profile , name WAF Editor , description Stages web-protection changes for review . Tick View monitoring , View protection , Edit protection , View appliances and View audit log . Leave Apply protection unticked. Save permissions . The table shows Effective role Operator (the profile grants a change permission) and 5 granted . Users → Add User jdoe , Profile WAF Editor , Create User . jdoe can now author web-protection changes but cannot push them to an appliance, and cannot see Settings administration, users or profiles.

The change takes effect on the user's next request: permissions are read from the assigned profile on every request, not cached in the session. Each action writes one audit entry: user.create , user.profile.set (with from and to ), user.enabled.set (with state ), user.reset_password , user.clear_2fa , user.unlock , user.delete , profile.create , profile.update and profile.clone (with the permission list or source), profile.delete . Saving a custom profile also updates the legacy role label ( Admin / Operator / Read Only ) of every user on it, which drives the role badges, the Operators counter

docs.h: "Refused: that change would remove the last administrator (no remaining user could manage users AND profiles)."
docs.x: Possible causes - You moved the last admin-capable user to a profile without users.manage or profiles.manage . - You removed one of those two permissions from the custom profile that all admin-capable users share. Solution 1. First give a second, active user a profile with both permissions (for example admin ). 2. Then repeat the change. Verification On Profiles , at least one profile with users assigned shows the admin-capable badge, and at least one of those users is Active .

docs.h: "Cannot delete the last remaining administrator." / "Cannot disable the last remaining administrator."
docs.x: Possible causes The account is the only active user who can manage both users and profiles. Solution Give another active account an admin-capable profile, then delete or disable this one. Verification The delete/disable succeeds with "User <name> deleted." / "User <name> disabled."

docs.h: "You cannot delete your own account." / "You cannot change your own account status."
docs.x: Possible causes You tried to act on your own account (only possible by posting directly; the table hides the buttons on your row). Solution Ask another administrator to do it.

docs.h: "“<name>” is assigned to N user(s). Reassign them first."
docs.x: Possible causes The profile still has users. Solution Use Change Profile on each of its users, then delete the profile. The Users column on Profiles shows when it reaches 0.
Possible causes Profile names are unique regardless of case: WAF editor clashes with WAF Editor . Solution Choose another name, or clone and rename.

docs.h: "System profiles are managed automatically and cannot be edited."
docs.x: Possible causes You tried to save a system profile. Solution Clone it and edit the copy, then assign the copy to users.

docs.h: "Username <name> already exists." / "Passwords do not match." / "The password must be at least 12 characters."
docs.x: Solution Pick another username, retype both password fields, or choose a password of 12 to 1024 characters.

docs.h: A user is told "Too many failed attempts — account temporarily locked. Try again later."
docs.x: Possible causes Ten consecutive failed sign-ins lock the account for 15 minutes, regardless of source address. Solution 1. An administrator clicks Unlock in the user's row (see Unlock an account ), or the user waits 15 minutes; a successful sign-in then clears the counter. 2. If no administrator can sign in, a root operator on the SATOM node can run sudo satom execute admin unlock <username> . It clears the lockout only; a disabled account stays disabled. The command writes an Audit Log entry with user cli/root . Verification The Locked badge is gone and the user signs in.

docs.h: Nobody can sign in as an administrator
docs.x: Solution On the SATOM node, as root: sudo satom execute admin reset-password <username> . The password is asked interactively (12 to 1024 characters, the same policy as the web forms) and never passed on the command line; the command also clears the lockout and re-enables the account, and writes an Audit Log entry with user cli/root . satom get user list shows who can log in. Verification The account signs in with the new password.

docs.h: A user sees "Forbidden" (403) on a page
docs.x: Possible causes Their profile lacks the permission the page needs. Solution Look up the page in Permissions , then add the key to the user's custom profile, or move the user to a profile that has it.

Advanced How permissions are resolved A profile stores granular keys ( area.action ). Most routes still check one of five legacy coarse keys ( view , backup , config_write , registry_edit , user_manage ). Holding any granular key listed for a coarse key grants that coarse key: for example any of Edit/Apply protection , Edit/Apply network , Run operations , the template keys or Edit/Run appliances grants config_write ; Manage users grants user_manage . The mapping is in Permissions . Because of that projection, granting one change permission (for example appliances.edit ) also opens every page

docs.k: settings admin console configuration administration tabs preferences admin console configuration page system settings preferences options users.manage profiles.manage advisor.configure
docs.s: Overview of the Settings page — called the Admin Console for administrators — with every group and tab, who can see it, and where each one is documented.

docs.x: Settings ( /settings/ ) is one page with a grouped side menu. For administrators the page is titled Admin Console and opens on General ; every other user sees a page titled Settings that contains only the My Account group and opens on Security . Administrator here means a profile that grants users.manage (the seeded admin profile, Administrator ). Ten of the eleven groups are shown only to administrators. My Account (Security, Change Password) is shown to every signed-in user ( Viewer and up). The Scout entry (the AI assistant) additionally requires advisor.configure , and the Profiles entry p

The menu is an accordion : all groups start collapsed, opening one group (or selecting a tab in it) folds the others, and the browser remembers the last group you opened. Each tab has a fixed address ( /settings/#tab-<name> ), so a bookmark or a link such as /settings/#tab-auth opens that tab directly. After a save, the page returns to the tab the form was on. An entry with the leaving arrow (↗) is a page , not a tab: Integrations replaces the console with its own page. Sentinel → Settings also exists as a standalone page, /settings/sentinel , with the same menu beside it; on that page the men

Group Tab What it does Who sees it Article System General Environment badge, default platform, timezone, bug-report opt-in, System Information, Libraries updater, Services (start/stop/restart units) Admin General System Software Update Repository The git repository this node downloads its own code from Admin Software update System Scout The AI assistant's switches and model providers (labelled AI Advisor until 2026-10-14) Admin with advisor.configure Scout settings System Integrations ↗ Separate page: NetBox, issue trackers, integration hooks Admin Integrations Source of Truth & Backup Configu

🔑 Permission Almost every save on this page checks users.manage (legacy key user_manage ) and answers 403 Forbidden without it — even if the address is typed directly. Scout (AI assistant) routes check advisor.configure . Sentinel → Settings and Path Diagnostics → Settings are saved with users.manage , like every other administrator tab. The standalone /settings/sentinel page opens for any user with a view permission, but its save answers 403 Forbidden without users.manage (see Sentinel settings ). Security and Change Password act only on your own account and need no permission. Independently

Almost every value on this page is stored in the database table app_settings , which is replicated to the standby node of a high-availability pair, so a value set on the primary applies to both. Exceptions are machine-specific actions such as Services and Libraries on General , which act on the node you are connected to (with an explicit option to include the peer). Secrets (passwords, tokens, API keys) are stored encrypted and are never shown again; a blank secret field always means keep the stored value .

Some values are not on this page even though they are configuration: Your top-bar banner and your interface language are personal and set on your profile page (see Users and profiles ). Naming patterns, the classification vocabulary and network segments have their own pages (see Naming , Classification and Segments ). Collection targets and cadence for metrics are on the Metrics pages. Scheduled actions (including the SoT harvest and the nightly system backup that Configuration SoT and Backup Server edit) are listed under Scheduled actions .
System backup — download and restore SATOM's own bundles. Audit log — every save on this page writes an audit entry ( settings.* ). Permissions — the full list of permission keys.

docs.k: general timezone environment prod badge dev badge libraries pip services systemctl restart system information update sources package index mirror pipeline nexus artifactory general configuration app settings service control restart satom python packages library update internal pypi mirror custom update feed update from internal pipeline users.manage
docs.s: The General tab of the Admin Console — installation-wide basics (environment badge, default platform, timezone), the bug-report opt-in, the System Information inventory, the per-package Libraries updater, the System packages installer, Update sources (where update packages and Python libraries come from) and the Services card that starts, stops and restarts this node's units.

docs.x: General is the first tab of the Admin Console (Settings → System → General). It holds the installation-wide basics — environment, default appliance platform, timezone — and three operational cards: System Information with its Libraries updater, and Services , which starts, stops and restarts the units this node runs without giving anyone a shell.

General Configuration form — stores a handful of installation-wide values in the replicated app_settings table (one value for every node of an HA pair). Bug report notifications — a personal opt-in: whether you receive bug reports filed by users (bell + email). System Information — read-only inventory: version, database, Python, operating system and the versions of the tracked libraries. Libraries — checks PyPI for newer versions of the tracked libraries and queues a per-package upgrade or rollback from a curated allowlist. It moves Python dependencies only; the application code is moved by So

An account whose profile grants users.manage . Libraries and Services act through the privileged updater service of each node. On a container (Docker) installation, Services shows the stack's containers when the operations agent is present and nothing otherwise; library changes are refused there because packages are baked into the image (see Container operations ).

🔑 Permission Every route behind this tab requires users.manage (legacy coarse key user_manage ). Users without it do not see the System group in the Settings menu at all, and a direct POST to /settings/general , /settings/services/action or /settings/library-pip returns 403 Forbidden . Typical holder: Administrator . The Bug report notifications card posts to /reports/prefs/notify , which is also gated on user_manage .

Open Settings → System → General . Edit the fields of the General Configuration card (see Configuration ). Click Save General Settings . The page reloads on the General tab with "General settings saved."

In the Bug report notifications card, switch on Receive bug reports from users (bell + email) . Click Save preference . The flash reads "Notification preference saved." The preference is personal (stored per user), default off .

docs.h: Check for and apply library updates
docs.x: In System Information → Libraries , click Check for updates . This is the only control that contacts PyPI ( https://pypi.org ); results are cached for 6 hours and the button forces a fresh check. The line under the heading then reads "All tracked libraries up to date · source pypi.org · checked …" or counts the outdated ones. A library PyPI did not answer for shows not checked , never a green tick, and the line says how many went unchecked. Upgrade and Rollback run pip in /opt/satom/venv . With an index set in Update sources , the check and the install both use it and the line names it; otherw

In System Information , under Libraries , find System packages . Each node has a column; a package that is not ok on every node shows an Install button. Click Install . With more than one node you are asked whether to install on all nodes (OK) or on this node only. The log box follows this node's install: the package manager it used (apt, dnf/yum, zypper or pacman), the install itself and a final sandbox works for satom check. A peer's own updater applies the request there; click Refresh to see its result.

Scroll to Update sources (under System Information). It has two columns, Update packages and Python libraries , and each is set on its own: you can change one and leave the other on Default . Set Source to Custom URL and enter the https:// URL: - Update packages : a latest.json in the same format as the public feed, for example https://pipeline.example.com/satom/latest.json . docs.h: Start, stop or restart a service
docs.x: Scroll to Services . The first section is this node ; each registered peer gets its own section, loaded separately so a dead standby never makes this node's card look broken. Click the action button on the unit's row and confirm. Buttons are state-aware: a running unit offers Restart and (if permitted) Stop ; a stopped unit offers Start , or Restart when restart is its only permitted action. The log box under the table follows the request until the runner reports the outcome. Click Refresh to re-read every unit's state.

The choices come from the ADOM registry; an invalid value is n

Page loads, Turbo navigation and every form submission count as activity. Background refreshes do not count: the notification bell, job progress, status badges, edit-lock heartbeats and other timed panel reloads. A tab left open therefore still locks. When the timeout has passed, the next request signs the session out and returns to the login page with "Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity." ; a script call gets a JSON 401 with session_locked: true . The lock is recorded in the Audit Log as session.idle_lock . Requests authenticated with an API token (Bearer) have no session a

🧪 Example — Stage a library upgrade on one node of an HA pair Open General on the primary and click Check for updates . Jinja2 shows Upgrade → 3.1.6 . Leave Also apply on the peer node(s) unticked. Confirm; watch the runner install, smoke-test and restart the web application. The drift table now reads Version DRIFT between nodes . After a day of normal use, open General again, tick the peer box and upgrade — the table returns to Nodes are level .

Saving the form writes the general.* keys and an audit entry settings.general . A service action writes settings.service_action (or settings.service_action.peer ); a library change writes settings.library_pip with the package, version, node and peer states. Restarting the web application kills the worker that served your click; the page reconnects and shows the runner's final log, including the health check.

Possible causes - The database rejected the write (for example a read-only standby node). Solution 1. Make the change on the primary node; settings replicate to the standby. Verification — the flash reads "General settings saved." and System Information shows the new values.

docs.h: "Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity."
docs.x: Possible causes - The browser session had no user activity for longer than Session Lock . Background refreshes do not keep a session alive. Solution 1. Sign in again; you return to the page you requested. 2. If the timeout is too short for your team, raise Session Lock (minutes) (up to 1440). Verification — the audit log shows session.idle_lock with the idle and configured minutes.

docs.h: "package '…' is not in the curated allowlist"
docs.x: Possible causes - The request named a package that is not on this node's curated list (the list is enforced by the web worker and again by the privileged runner). Solution — only the packages shown in the Libraries table can be changed from here.

Possible causes - bwrap: No permissions to create new namespace (or similar): the kernel or the container does not let the service account create user namespaces (an LXC without nesting, or a sysctl such as kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0 ). - bwrap: execvp /usr/bin/true: No such file or directory on SLES / openSUSE Leap 15: SATOM versions before the SA-0002 fix assumed a usr-merged system and hid the real /lib64 , which holds the program loader on SUSE 15. Solution — for the first, allow user namespaces for the node and click Install again (an installed package only re-runs the check). For

docs.h: "pypi.org is not reachable from this node: versions were NOT checked"
docs.x: Possible causes — this node has no route to pypi.org: an offline (air-gapped) install, a proxy, or no DNS. No version was compared, so the card offers no Upgrade . Solution — on an offline node this is expected: its libraries move with the signed update package (Software Update & HA, see Offline updates ). Each package carries the wheels for that release's requirements.txt and installs them with --no-index , so applying it brings every library to the version the release pins. On a node that should be online, check outbound HTTPS. The rest of the page is unaffected because the check never runs

docs.h: "… cannot be used: the token is stored in the vault, which could not be read: …"
docs.x: Possible causes — an update source is set with a user and token, but the token cannot be read (the vault is sealed or unreachable, or the local key changed). Solution — fix the vault (Settings → Vault → Test connection), or save the source again with the token. SATOM refuses the check, the download and the library change until then; it never falls back to the public default without saying so.

docs.h: "HTTP 401: the index wants credentials, or refused the ones given"
docs.x: Possible causes — the source needs authentication and none was given, or the user or token was rejected. A token without the registry's package-read permission fails the same way. Solution — set User + token , check the token's scopes on the registry, and click Test again.

docs.h: "Update check failed: SATOM did not answer the request."
docs.x: Possible causes — the check endpoint itself failed (the web service was restarting, or the session expired). Solution — reload the page and click Check for updates again.

docs.h: A Services action says "… is not allowed on '…' from this console"
docs.x: Possible causes — the action is not in the unit's policy (for example Stop on the web application, nginx or PostgreSQL). Solution — use Restart , or act from a shell if you really need to stop the unit.

Possible causes — the request directory for the privileged runner is not writable, or the runner is not installed. Solution — check the updater units with the CLI and the services and timers reference.

Advanced Where things are stored and how requests run General values live in app_settings under general.app_name , general.env_mode , general.default_kind , general.timezone , general.session_timeout , general.log_format and general.log_levels (JSON list). The former general.poll_interval and general.show_raw_config keys may still exist in the table; nothing reads or writes them. The Session Lock value is cached for 30 seconds per worker and the cache is cleared on save. The last-activity time is stored in the signed session cookie. The bug-report opt-in is a per-user setting, default "0" . Th

docs.s: Turn Scout, the AI assistant (formerly AI Advisor), on, decide whether it may call read-only tools and external providers, and manage the provider registry (Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic) with a test call before saving.

docs.x: The Scout tab configures the Scout AI chat: three feature switches and the list of model providers it may use. The assistant never writes to SATOM or an appliance directly. Local Ollama traffic stays on your network; anything sent to an external provider — the new message and the earlier conversation turns sent with it — is redacted of known internal identifiers first and recorded in the Audit log as advisor.send . An Ollama provider counts as local only when its Base URL host is localhost , a loopback, link-local or private address; an Ollama provider on a public or unresolvable host is treat

Enable Scout — feature master switch (default off). Allow read-only tool calls (mode C) — lets the model call read-only tools (default off). Allow external providers — a second gate, required in addition to a configured external provider (default off). Providers — add, edit, delete, test and choose the default provider. Each switch saves immediately when toggled.

advisor.configure and administrator rights ( users.manage ): the entry sits in the admin-only System group and is additionally hidden from administrators without advisor.configure . A reachable model: a local Ollama host, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint or the Anthropic API.
🔑 Permission All /settings/ai/* routes require advisor.configure ; without it they return 403 and the menu entry is not shown. Chatting with Scout needs advisor.use (see Scout ).
Open Settings → System → Scout . Switch on Enable Scout . Leave the other two switches off to keep everything on your network.

Click Add provider . Fill Key (slug, unique) , Label , Kind , Base URL , Model and, for external providers, API key . Click Test connection . One trivial chat call is made with the form's current values (not yet saved): "OK — <the model's reply>" or "Failed — <error>" . When editing with a blank API key, the stored key is used. Click Save . The provider appears in the list; the first provider, or the one you mark with Make default , carries the default badge.
Edit opens the form; the key cannot be changed; a blank API key keeps the stored one. Delete asks Delete provider "<key>"? and also removes its stored API key.

Field Description Required Example Key (slug, unique) Identifier; saving an existing key replaces that provider. Yes openai-corp Label Display name; blank = the key. No Corporate gateway Kind Ollama (local, no API key) , OpenAI-compatible (ChatGPT / Azure OpenAI / LiteLLM / vLLM…) , Anthropic (Claude Messages API) . Yes OpenAI-compatible Base URL Endpoint; a trailing / is removed. For an Ollama provider, the host decides whether it counts as local (loopback, link-local, private address or localhost ) or external (any other host). Yes https://llm.example.com/v1 Model Model name as the provider

🧪 Example — Local first, external on request Add ollama-lab (Ollama, http://{ip}:11434 — a private address, so it counts as local; model qwen2.5-coder:32b ), test, save, Make default . Add claude (Anthropic) with an API key but leave Allow external providers off; users can only chat locally until you switch that gate on.

Flags and providers are stored in app_settings ( ai.enabled , ai.tools_enabled , ai.external_allowed , ai.default_provider , ai.providers ); each API key is stored encrypted under its own key. Changes apply to the next chat message.
Solution — fill Key (slug, unique) before saving.
Solution — choose one of the three kinds in the list.

Possible causes — wrong Base URL or model name, missing or invalid API key, or the host is unreachable from the SATOM node. A large local model can take a long time to load on a cold call. Solution — correct the values and test again; for Ollama, check the model is pulled on the host.

docs.h: Users get "external providers are disabled -- turn on \"Allow external providers\" …"
docs.x: Possible causes — the default (or chosen) provider is external and Allow external providers is off. Solution — switch the gate on, or make a local provider the default.

docs.h: An Ollama provider is treated as external
docs.x: Possible causes — its Base URL host is a public address, a public DNS name, or a name the SATOM node cannot resolve. Only localhost and loopback, link-local or private addresses count as local. Solution — point Base URL at the Ollama host's private address (or a name that resolves to one), or keep it external and switch Allow external providers on. Verification — chatting with that provider no longer reports that external providers are disabled while the gate is off.

Advanced Notes The test call is never stored or exported; it uses a 20-second timeout. Deleting the default provider makes the first remaining provider the default. This tab loads its own state from /settings/ai/state , so it works independently of the rest of the Settings page.

docs.k: source of truth sot snapshot change log retention evacuate harvest device_sync config history config history configuration versions sot retention free disk space harvest interval users.manage
docs.s: How much configuration-snapshot payload and change log each node keeps locally (per ADOM), how to free local space on demand, and how often the fleet harvest that creates new SoT versions runs.

docs.x: The Configuration SoT (source of truth) is SATOM's versioned history of every managed appliance's configuration . This tab decides how much of that history stays on the node's own disk, moves the rest to the Backup Server , and sets how often the fleet is harvested. It is the only thing SATOM calls a source of truth — backups, the software update repository and firmware images are deliberately separate.

Explains the store and shows its current size: versions, how many still have payload on this node, how many are evacuated , number of blobs and MB. Holds a house rule (all ADOMs) and one card per active ADOM with three numbers: newest versions kept locally, days of payload kept locally, days of change log kept in the database. Lists inactive ADOMs that still carry a rule or a history , with a Clear the override button. Free space on this node now — uploads missing snapshots and change-log months to the backup server, then deletes locally only what the server is confirmed to hold. Refresh frequ
users.manage . A configured Backup Server . Without one, nothing can leave the node: the evacuation card says "no backup server is configured, so nothing can leave this node" .

🔑 Permission All four actions ( POST /settings/sot , /settings/sot/evacuate , /settings/sot/refresh ) require users.manage (coarse user_manage ). Without it the Source of Truth & Backup group is not in the menu and a direct POST returns 403 .

Open Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Configuration SoT . In the card All ADOMs (house rule) , fill Newest versions kept locally , Days of payload kept locally and Days of change log kept in the database . Click Save . The flash confirms the effective numbers, e.g. "SoT policy saved for every ADOM: newest 2 version(s) and 1 day(s) of snapshot stay on this node, and 365 day(s) of change log. …"

In the ADOM's card (badge with the ADOM key), fill one or more boxes. Empty boxes show the value in force as a placeholder. Click Save . Under each box, In force says which level answered: set for this ADOM , inherited from the house rule or product default . To remove the override, clear all three boxes and save — the ADOM inherits again. This is the only way to undo an ADOM override.

In Free space on this node now , read the archive path and the last run. Click Upload and free space now . The flash reports what was pushed, evacuated and archived, or "Nothing was evacuated: …" with the reason.

In Refresh frequency , set Harvest every (minutes) . Click Save frequency . The flash reads "Configuration SoT now refreshes every N minutes." or, when no interval harvest existed, "Created a fleet-wide SoT harvest every N minutes." The next run is recomputed immediately, so a shorter interval applies now.

Field Description Required Example Newest versions kept locally Snapshots per device always kept on this node regardless of age. Default 2 (a diff needs a version and the one before it). Range 1–10000; out-of-range values are clamped; 0 , blank (house card) or non-numeric mean the default. No 2 Days of payload kept locally Snapshots younger than this stay local whatever the version count says. Default 1 . Range 1–36500, clamped. The two payload numbers are a union : a snapshot stays if it is in the newest N or younger than D days. No 7 Days of change log kept in the database How long version r

🧪 Example — FortiAnalyzer snapshots fill the disk FortiAnalyzer configurations are large. Keep the house rule at 2 versions / 1 day, and in the fortianalyzer card set Newest versions kept locally to 1 . Save, then click Upload and free space now . Older FortiAnalyzer snapshots move to the backup server; opening one later downloads it again transparently.

Policies are stored per scope in app_settings ; an audit entry settings.sot_local_policy is written with the effective numbers. Upload and free space now writes settings.sot_evacuate . Save frequency edits (or creates) the device_sync scheduled action — not a settings key — and writes settings.sot_refresh . The card links to that row in Scheduled actions and warns in red when it is DISABLED, so nothing is harvested on a schedule right now . Archived change-log months land under <System bundles path>/sot-log/ on the backup server.

Possible causes — the posted ADOM key is not in the ADOM registry (for example it was deleted after the page was loaded). Solution — reload the page and save from a card that is listed. Verification — the flash starts with "SoT policy saved for …" .

docs.h: "Nothing was evacuated: push failed, nothing evacuated: …"
docs.x: Possible causes - The backup server is unreachable or its credentials are wrong. - No backup server is configured. Solution 1. Open Backup Server , save correct credentials, click Test connection . 2. Run Upload and free space now again. Verification — the store line shows a higher evacuated count. ℹ️ Note — Safe by design A listing that fails is read as "nothing is off-box", never as permission to delete, so a broken server can never cause local history to be lost.

docs.h: The harvest interval does not seem to apply
docs.x: Possible causes - The device_sync row is disabled (the card says so in red). - The harvest you are thinking of is a wall-clock schedule (for example "daily at 02:00"). Those are reported as Other harvest schedules exist and are NOT changed by this field and must be edited in Automation. Solution — enable or edit the row in Scheduled actions .

docs.h: A month of change log is not archived
docs.x: Possible causes — only months lying entirely outside the log window are archived, and a month whose snapshots are not yet off-box is held whole. Solution — run Upload and free space now after the snapshots have been pushed; check Last run … month(s) held on the card.

Advanced Keys and internals Payload keys: sot.local_versions , sot.local_days ; log window: sot.log_keep_days . Per-ADOM overrides append .<adom> (for example sot.local_versions.fortianalyzer ). The last archive outcome is stored in sot.log_archive_last so the page never makes an SFTP call to render. For the payload keys a stored 0 or malformed value reads as unset ; for the log key 0 is a real value (never trim). Snapshots are gzip blobs under data/sot/objects/ , content-addressed by hash; the index lives in PostgreSQL. An evacuated version keeps its row with evacuated_at set; opening it fetc

docs.s: The external SFTP server that device config backups, SATOM's own system bundles, archived firmware and off-box SoT data are copied to — plus the hour the system bundle is written and how many bundles stay on the node.

docs.x: The Backup Server tab configures the SFTP box that several separate streams are copied to . It is a destination, not an authority: nothing stored there decides what a device is configured to do — that is the Configuration SoT . The same tab sets when this node writes its own system bundle and how many bundles it keeps locally.

Stream Written by Path field Device config backups the appliances themselves , on their own schedule ( config system backup ); SATOM reads, indexes and diffs them Config backups path System bundles this node's scheduled system_backup action (PostgreSQL dump + JSON tree + SoT blobs), and a manual Create backup now on System backup when its push box is ticked System bundles path Firmware archive images archived when they leave local storage Firmware archive path SoT change-log archive the Configuration SoT evacuation <System bundles path>/sot-log/ ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: a manual bundle from
users.manage . An SFTP account on the backup server. Paths are as seen inside the SFTP session (the server typically chroots the backup user).

🔑 Permission Every action on this tab ( POST /settings/backup-server , /backup-server/test , /backup-server/schedule , /backup-server/bundle-retention , /backup-server/bundle-evict ) requires users.manage . Without it the group is not shown and direct calls return 403 .

Open Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server . Fill Host , Port , Username , Password and the three paths. Click Save backup server settings — "Backup server settings saved." Click Test connection . On success it shows connected to <host>:<port> — N device folder(s) under <config path>, M file(s) under <firmware path> . ❗ Important — Test uses the saved values Test connection reads the stored settings, not the values currently typed in the form, and lists only the config-backups and firmware paths. Save first, then test.

In System bundle schedule , set Daily, at (HH:MM). The time is wall-clock in the console timezone printed under the field (set on General ). Click Save bundle schedule . The flash reads "System bundles are now written at HH:MM <timezone>." or, if nothing was scheduled, "Created a nightly system backup at HH:MM <timezone>."

In Local bundle retention , set Bundles kept on this node . Click Save bundle retention . The flash reads "System bundles: keeping N on this node after a verified upload. …" To apply it immediately, click Evict verified bundles now in Apply bundle retention now .

Field Description Required Example Host SFTP server name or address. The server counts as configured only when Host and Username are set. Yes backup.example.com Port Default 22 ; clamped to 1–65535, invalid → 22. No 22 Username SFTP user. Yes satom-backup Password Stored Fernet-encrypted, never shown back. Leave blank to keep the current one (placeholder Leave blank to keep current ). First time — Config backups path One sub-folder per appliance, named as the device is named in SATOM. Default /configs . No /configs Firmware archive path Default /firmware . No /firmware System bundles path Defa

🧪 Example — Keep one local bundle for fast restores Set Bundles kept on this node to 1 and save. After the next successful upload, all but the newest verified bundle are removed locally. A bundle the server does not hold at the same size is always kept, whatever the number says.

Credentials and paths are stored in app_settings ( backup_server.config , password encrypted); audit entry settings.backup_server . Save bundle schedule edits (or creates, enabled with catch-up) the daily system_backup scheduled action with push_server on, recomputes its next run and writes settings.system_backup_schedule . The card shows the driving action, its last status and next run in UTC, and DISABLED, so this node is writing no bundles at all right now when the row is off. Retention runs automatically after every successful upload; Evict verified bundles now runs it on demand and upload

docs.h: "backup server not configured (Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server)"
docs.x: Possible causes — Host or Username is empty in the saved settings. Solution — fill both on this tab and click Save backup server settings before testing.

docs.h: Test connection fails with an authentication or socket error
docs.x: Possible causes — wrong password, port, or firewall between the node and the server; the config or firmware path does not exist inside the chroot. Solution 1. Correct and save the values (a blank password keeps the stored one). 2. Make sure both Config backups path and Firmware archive path exist on the server. Verification — the green line lists the device folders and firmware files found.

docs.h: "This node backs up on a … schedule, which one hour cannot express — change it in Automation rather than adding a second nightly bundle."
docs.x: Possible causes — the existing system_backup row is weekly, interval or another non-daily kind. The field is disabled and the save is refused so that no second bundle is scheduled. Solution — edit the row in Scheduled actions , or change it to a daily schedule there.

docs.h: "Nothing removed. N kept by policy, M not verified on the backup server (K bundle(s) known off-box)."
docs.x: Possible causes — bundles were never uploaded, or the server copy has a different size. Solution — check the upload status of the latest system_backup run; fix the credentials and let the next run upload.

Possible causes — the appliance is not pushing its own backups. SATOM does not author device backups; it can report the gap but not fill it. Solution — configure the scheduled backup on the appliance (see Backups ).

Advanced Internals Bundle eviction deletes a local bundle only when the server listing shows it at the same size ; downloading or restoring an off-box bundle fetches it back first (see System backup ). When the hour field creates the schedule, the new action is named Nightly system backup (Postgres + JSON) ; rename it in Automation if you like. The three save buttons post to separate endpoints on purpose, so changing the hour or the retention never rewrites the SFTP credentials.

docs.s: Choose which directories (Active Directory, LDAP, FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS) may sign users in and in what order, what profile new directory users get, whether they need approval, and import directory users before their first sign-in.

docs.x: The Authentication tab decides who can prove their identity to SATOM. Besides the local user database (always on), you can enable Active Directory, generic LDAP and FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS as sign-in sources, give them an order, set what happens to a directory user the first time they sign in, and import directory users in advance.

Sign-in sources — the local database (always on, not configurable) plus any of Active Directory , LDAP (generic) and FortiAuthenticator / RADIUS , each with an Order . Sign-in walks the enabled sources in order; the first that accepts the password wins. Default profile and approval gate for directory users created at first sign-in. Connection settings for the LDAP server (shared by AD and LDAP) and for RADIUS. Import scopes — groups/OUs to import, each with the profile its members receive. Test connection — tests one source with the values currently in the form. Sync directory users — imports

users.manage . For AD/LDAP: a reachable LDAP server; for LDAP (generic) a service account (Bind DN) that can search users. For FortiAuthenticator/RADIUS: a RADIUS client entry for SATOM on the FortiAuthenticator, and — for importing users — the FortiAuthenticator registered under Appliances (its API key is reused to read the roster; see FortiAuthenticator ).

🔑 Permission Saving, testing and syncing ( POST /settings/auth , /settings/auth/test , /settings/auth/sync ) require users.manage . Users without it do not see the Access & Identity group; direct requests return 403 .

Open Settings → Access & Identity → Authentication . Under Sign-in sources , tick Active Directory , LDAP (generic) and/or FortiAuthenticator / RADIUS and set each one's Order (1–9). The connection blocks for the ticked sources appear below. Fill the connection fields (see Configuration ). Set Default profile for new directory users and decide on Require administrator approval for new directory users . Click Save authentication settings — "Authentication settings saved." 💡 Tip — Order matters An unreachable source burns its whole timeout before the next one is tried, and every source ahead of

In Test connection , pick the Source to test (one at a time). Optionally type a test username and test password to verify a full bind. Click Test connection . The result shows in green or red. Values are taken from the form, unsaved; a blank secret field falls back to the stored secret.

Add rows under Sync groups / OU DNs (AD/LDAP) or the FortiAuthenticator group table (RADIUS), each with an optional Profile on import (blank = the default profile). No rows means every user the directory exposes. Save the settings first. Click Sync directory users . On success you are taken to Users with a flash such as "12 new user(s) imported as disabled (pending approval); 3 already existed." Enable each imported user (and adjust the profile) under Users .

Field Description Required Example Sign-in sources → Enabled Tick the external sources to use. None ticked = local only. No AD Order Position in the sign-in chain, 1–9. A missing or invalid value keeps the source's submitted position. No 1 Default profile for new directory users Profile name given to a directory user created at first sign-in (and to imported users whose group row has no profile). Default readonly ; a blank value saves readonly . An unknown name falls back to the default, then readonly — never to a more privileged profile. The placeholder shows readonly . No readonly Require ad

docs.s: Restrict the source IP addresses or networks from which non-administrators may use SATOM; administrators and loopback are always allowed so a typo cannot lock you out.

docs.x: Access Control holds one gate: the IP Whitelist . When it contains entries, only sessions coming from those source addresses or networks can use SATOM. It answers where a session may come from; who may sign in is decided by the directory, the approval gate and the profile.

Stores a list of IP addresses or CIDR networks, each with a free-text note. Enforces it on every request of a signed-in non-administrator : a request from any other address is refused with 403 Forbidden . Empty list = no restriction. Administrators (holders of users.manage ) are always exempt, and the sign-in pages and static files are never blocked, so the people who manage the list cannot lock themselves out. Shows a card Who may sign in explaining that there is no per-username allowlist, and — if an older installation still stores one — offers Clear the leftover list .
users.manage . If SATOM sits behind a reverse proxy, the client address must be passed through so the gate sees the real source IP (see Security model ).

🔑 Permission POST /settings/access requires users.manage ; POST /settings/access/clear-legacy-allowlist checks the same capability inside the view. Without it the tab is not shown and requests return 403 .

Open Settings → Access & Identity → Access Control . Click Add IP for each address or network and fill IP / CIDR and Note . Remove a row with the bin icon. Click Save Access Control . The flash reads "Access control saved." ; invalid entries are dropped with "Skipped invalid IP/CIDR(s): …" .

If the card Who may sign in shows "This install still stores N name(s) from the removed allowlist …" , click Clear the leftover list . The flash reads "Cleared N leftover username(s) from the removed allowlist." Those names were no longer enforced.

Field Description Required Example IP / CIDR An IPv4/IPv6 address or network. Validated on save (host bits are allowed: 192.0.2.10/24 is accepted). Invalid values are skipped with a warning. Blank rows are ignored. No 192.0.2.0/24 Note Free text describing the entry. No office VPN

🧪 Example — Allow only the operations network Add 198.51.100.0/24 (note ops LAN ) and 203.0.113.7 (note jump host ) and save. An operator connecting from home without VPN now receives 403 on every page; an administrator can still sign in from anywhere to fix the list.

The list is stored in app_settings ( access.ip_whitelist ) and replicated to the standby. Each save writes the audit entry settings.access with the number of entries. Refused requests are logged in the application log as ACCESS_DENY reason=ip_not_whitelisted with user, IP and endpoint.
Possible causes — a typo, a range written as a-b , or a hostname instead of an address. Solution — enter single addresses or CIDR networks only, then save again.

docs.h: An operator gets 403 Forbidden on every page
docs.x: Possible causes — the operator's source IP is not on the list, or a proxy in front of SATOM replaces the client address. Solution 1. Find the refused address in the application log line ACCESS_DENY reason=ip_not_whitelisted . 2. Add it (or its network) and save. Verification — the operator can open pages again without signing in anew.

Possible causes — the stored access configuration cannot be read (for example a hand-edited or half-written database row). SATOM refuses to serve non-administrators rather than treat an unreadable list as "allow everyone"; the log shows ACCESS_DENY reason=access_config_unreadable . Solution — sign in as an administrator (exempt), open this tab and click Save Access Control to rewrite the list.

Advanced How the gate works The check runs before every request of an authenticated user. Endpoints static , the service and upload workers, and everything under auth. are always reachable. Administrators return before the list is read at all. The former per-username allowlist ( access.allowed_users ) is no longer enforced; the profile, the directory group filter and the approval gate on Authentication decide who may sign in.

docs.s: Optionally keep appliance passwords, directory secrets and integration-hook secrets in an external OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault (KV v2) instead of, or in addition to, the local encrypted database — and migrate or remove the local copies safely.

docs.x: By default every credential SATOM holds — appliance passwords, the directory bind password, the FortiAuthenticator shared secret, integration-hook secrets — is encrypted with a local key and stored in SATOM's database. The Vault tab adds an external OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault (KV v2 API) so the key material no longer sits on the same host as the data it protects. Nothing changes until you turn it on: Store in SATOM only remains the default.

Three storage modes for new secrets: Store in SATOM only (Fernet) — default; the vault is not used. Store in both — read vault first, fall back to SATOM — migration mode; nothing breaks if the vault is down, but the local copy still exists. Store in the vault only — closes the exposure; a vault outage makes credentials unavailable. Test connection — checks reachability, seal state, authentication and mount access. Migrate existing credentials — copies every stored appliance password, the RADIUS shared secret, the LDAP/AD bind password, the alert webhook signing secret (to alerts/webhook ) and

users.manage . A KV v2 mount on the vault and either an AppRole (role_id + secret_id) or a static token with read/write access to it. The vault's TLS certificate trusted by the node (system trust store or the CA certificate field).
🔑 Permission All four endpoints ( POST /settings/vault , /vault/test , /vault/migrate , /vault/scrub ) require users.manage . Without it the Access & Identity group is hidden and calls return 403 .

Fill Vault address , KV v2 mount , Authentication and its credentials, then click Save (leave Use an external vault off for now if you only want to test). Click Test connection . The Status card shows ✓ Vault <version> reachable, unsealed, mount 'sa

Default Store in SATOM only (Fernet) . No Store in both Vault address Base URL; a trailing / is removed. Must be an http:// or https:// URL: any other scheme (for example file:// ) is refused on every vault request. When enabled https://vault.example.com:8200 KV v2 mount Mount path. Default satom . No satom Authentication AppRole (default) or Static token . Yes AppRole Namespace (optional) Vault Enterprise

Because Store in both reads the vault first and falls back to the local copy, a vault hiccup during migration cannot take appliances offline. Only after Copy to vault reports 0 failed switch to Store in the vault only , then scrub.

docs.h: "A vault address is required before enabling the vault."
docs.x: Solution — fill Vault address , then save with the switch on.
Possible causes — Migrate was run before an address and complete credentials were saved. Solution — complete and Save the form; the Status badge must read configured .

docs.h: "The vault is not the authoritative store. Set the mode to “Store in the vault only” before removing local copies."
docs.x: Solution — finish migration, switch the mode to vault-only and save, then run the scrub.

docs.h: Test reports "Unreachable: the vault address must be an http(s) URL (got '…')"
docs.x: Possible causes — Vault address uses a scheme other than http or https . The address is saved as typed; the check runs on every request SATOM sends to the vault, so the vault stays unusable until it is corrected. Solution — enter the address as https://<host>:8200 (or http:// for a lab vault), save and click Test connection again.

docs.h: Test reports "The vault is reachable but SEALED — it cannot answer for secrets."
docs.x: Solution — unseal the vault, then test again.

docs.h: Test reports "Reachable, but authentication failed: …" or "Authenticated, but mount '…' is not readable: …"
docs.x: Solution — check the role_id/secret_id or token and that its policy grants access to the KV v2 mount; save and test again. Test connection uses the saved configuration.

docs.h: A scrub item reports "no copy in the vault - the local one is the last one"
docs.x: Possible causes — that credential was never migrated or the vault copy differs. The local copy is kept on purpose. Solution — run Copy to vault again, then repeat the scrub.

Advanced Paths, markers and caveats When the vault owns a secret, the local column holds an encrypted marker instead of the password, so older code paths see a readable placeholder rather than an empty value. Directory secrets live at auth/fortiauthenticator (field shared_secret ) and auth/ldap (field bind_password ) under the mount. A new Bind password typed on Authentication is written to the vault and, unless the vault is the only store, to the local database too — the same path as the FortiAuthenticator shared secret — so sign-in, which reads the vault copy first, uses the new value. docs.s: The resolver list behind the DNS & LB Lookup tool, and the registry of IPAM/DDI backends (EfficientIP, phpIPAM, NetBox) that SATOM uses to reserve addresses and publish DNS records.

docs.x: The Network & DNS group has two tabs: DNS Lookup — the DNS servers that the DNS & LB Lookup tool queries. Every enabled server becomes one column in the lookup results; all ADOMs share the list. DNS Records — the registry of IPAM / DDI backends : the systems SATOM may use to hand out addresses ( IPAM role) and publish names ( DNS role). More than one backend is supported, each with its own roles, scope, priority and credential. Provisioning, the Server Policy wizard and ACME dns-01 challenges use it.

DNS Lookup : stores a list of name + server rows, each individually enabled. DNS Records : add, edit, enable/disable, test and delete backends. When a request needs a backend it is chosen as follows: 1 Role only backends carrying the IPAM or DNS role asked for 2 Most specific scope sub.example.com beats example.com; an unscoped backend answers anything but ranks last 3 Priority equal scope: the lowest priority number wins 4 Tie equal scope and equal priority is refused and both backends are named Pools are matched exactly , never by network containment: {ip}/16 does not cover {ip}/22 . Zones a
users.manage . For a backend: its API URL and a credential (EfficientIP password, phpIPAM API app token or NetBox API token).

🔑 Permission All routes ( POST /settings/dns-tool , /settings/dns-records/* ) require users.manage . Without it the Network & DNS group is hidden and calls return 403 . Using the DNS & LB Lookup tool itself is covered in DNS tool .

Open Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup . Edit existing rows or fill one of the three empty rows ( Name , Server (IP / hostname) , Enabled ). To remove a server, clear its row. Click Save DNS servers . The flash reads "DNS server list saved (N servers)." and the page returns to the DNS Lookup tab. ℹ️ Note Changed in 2.11.0: saving the resolver list returns to the DNS Lookup tab; before, the page opened on the first tab of the console. Need more than three new servers? Save, and three new empty rows appear.

Open Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Records . Under Add a backend , fill Name , choose Provider , set Priority and Enabled . Tick the Roles : IPAM — hands out addresses and/or DNS — publishes records . A role the provider can never perform is disabled (phpIPAM shows This provider has no record CRUD in any installation. ). Optionally restrict the scope: DNS zones this backend serves and IPAM pools this backend serves , one per line. Empty = catch-all. Fill the provider fields and the secret; keep Verify the certificate on. Click Test these values (tests the form without saving), then Save backe

Edit loads the row into the form (secret left blank = keep the stored one). Test probes the saved row and records the result ( OK / error ) in the table. Disable / Enable toggles the row without deleting it. Delete asks Delete the backend "<name>"? .

New rows are ticked by default. No on

Provider Fields EfficientIP SOLIDserver Base URL , Username , DNS server (smart/appliance name) , Default DNS view (optional) , Default zone (used when a caller names none) , Default IPAM pool (subnet id or name) phpIPAM Base URL , API app id , Default IPAM pool (subnet id or CIDR) NetBox Base URL , Default zone (used when a caller names none) , Default IPAM pool (prefix id or CIDR) A default zone or pool must lie inside the declared scope (if a scope is declared); otherwise the save is refused.

🧪 Example — Split IPAM and DNS ipam-main : phpIPAM, role IPAM only, pools 42 and 198.51.100.0/24 , priority 100. ddi-dns : EfficientIP, role DNS only, zones example.com , priority 100. ddi-lab : EfficientIP, role DNS only, zones lab.example.com , priority 100. A record for www.lab.example.com goes to ddi-lab (more specific scope); www.example.com goes to ddi-dns ; an address from pool 42 comes from ipam-main .

The resolver list is stored in app_settings ( dnstool.servers ); audit settings.dns_tool . Backends are rows of their own; audit entries settings.dns_backend.save , .toggle , .delete , .test . The last test result and error are kept on the row and shown in the table and on the Server Policy wizard's selector. Allocations and records remember which backend created them, so a rollback goes back to that backend.
Solution — enter an IP address or a plain hostname without scheme, port suffix or spaces.

docs.h: "A backend with neither role can never answer anything. Give it the IPAM role, the DNS role, or both — or delete it."
docs.x: Solution — tick at least one role.

docs.h: "phpIPAM has no DNS record CRUD in any installation, so it cannot carry the DNS role. …"
docs.x: Solution — keep phpIPAM for addresses and point the DNS role at EfficientIP or NetBox.

docs.x: Solution — type the secret when adding or when testing an unsaved backend.
Solution — choose a unique name.

docs.x: Solution — add the default zone to the scope, or clear the default. The same rule applies to the default pool.

docs.h: "N provisioning run(s) still hold this backend as the handle for the address or record they created. …"
docs.x: Possible causes — unfinished provisioning runs reference the backend for rollback. Solution — finish or abort those runs in Provisioning , then delete.

docs.h: Lookup or provisioning says no backend matches
docs.x: Possible causes — no enabled backend carries the role ( no backend ), backends exist but none claims the zone or pool and none is a catch-all ( no match ), or two backends tie on scope and priority ( ambiguous ). Solution — register a backend, widen a scope, or change one priority. A fleet with no DDI is supported: publishing a name then only warns.

Advanced Upgrade and storage notes An older single-provider configuration ( dnsrecords.* settings) is folded into one unscoped backend on first start; its default zone and pool are kept as defaults, not as a scope. The Test button on a saved row also records the provider's live capabilities (for example whether NetBox has netbox-dns). Backend secrets are encrypted with the node key; they are not routed through the Vault .

docs.s: Register the Proxmox VE and VMware ESXi hosts SATOM may build appliance virtual machines on, and test what each host actually permits before a provisioning run depends on it.

docs.x: The Hypervisors tab is the registry of virtualization hosts on which SATOM may create appliance virtual machines during provisioning . Proxmox VE and VMware ESXi are supported, and you can register several of each. With no hypervisor registered, the machine-creation part of provisioning is hidden entirely; the rest of the pipeline (address, DNS, certificate, configuration profile) still works against a machine you built by hand.

Stores each target's endpoint, credentials (encrypted, never sent back to the browser) and placement defaults. Test connects, then reports the host's real capabilities: create VM, power, upload image, attach disk, serial console — and lists what blocks an unattended ( Full ) run. Shows each target's status: ready , read-only API , error or untested . What each backend can do, as the tab explains it: Capability Proxmox VE VMware ESXi Create / power / delete Yes, over the REST API Licence-dependent: the free edition makes the vSphere API read-only; otherwise SATOM falls back to the host shell Up

The concept is explained in ADOMs and products .

docs.x: Possible causes — global , fortiweb and fortiadc are wired into URL scoping. Solution — switch Active off instead.

docs.x: Policy Links are custom links rendered at the top of every Server Policy detail page. docs.h: "Skipped a row missing its URL." / "Skipped a row missing its label."
docs.x: Solution — fill both fields or clear the row. If no row could be saved you also see "No links were saved — see the message(s) above. Each link needs both a label and a URL."

docs.h: "Note: '…' uses {…}, which no policy fills — it will appear literally. Valid tokens: …"
docs.x: Solution — fix the token name; the link is saved anyway.

docs.h: "Only the first 10 links were kept (limit reached)."
docs.x: Solution — remove links you no longer need; the maximum is ten.

docs.h: A link does not appear on a policy page
docs.x: Possible causes — the link is disabled, or it uses a token the policy has no value for. Solution — check Enabled , or remove the token the policy lacks.

Advanced Notes Checkbox state is matched to rows by a per-row token, so adding and removing rows in any order keeps each link's flags with it. Validation is deliberately permissive: only rows missing a label or a URL are dropped.
